articles.title: Cardi B and Stefon Diggs’ baby breaks the internet with nearly 59 million views
articles.summary: Cardi B has finally given fans a proper look at the little boy she shares with Stefon Diggs and the internet clearly cannot get enough of him.
articles.body: Cardi B has finally given fans a proper look at the little boy she shares with Stefon Diggs and the internet clearly cannot get enough of him. The rapper's adorable birthday reveal has reportedly approached 59 million views on Instagram, turning what was already a special family milestone into a viral moment.Cardi celebrated her son's first birthday on November 4 by sharing a collection of pictures and videos, finally introducing fans to the little boy she and Diggs had largely kept away from the public eye for the past year. And she did not just reveal his face. She also shared his name.Cardi B finally introduces Grey Marsean Diggs to the worldThe Grammy-winning rapper revealed that her youngest son is named Grey Marsean Diggs, giving fans their first proper glimpse of the little boy."Happy 1st birthday to Grey Marsean Diggs," Cardi wrote in her Instagram caption.The birthday carousel featured Grey looking adorable in different outfits. One picture showed him wearing a green baseball cap, a white T-shirt and a little chain around his neck. Another featured him in a doctor costume, seemingly paying tribute to the popular medical drama Grey's Anatomy.But it was the sheer reach of the post that caught everyone's attention. An Instagram insights screenshot shared online showed the birthday post approaching 58.7 million views. Cardi also reacted to the response, writing that almost 59 million views was crazy and expressing how loved her little boy was.Considering she had kept his face and name private for almost an entire year, it is easy to understand why fans were so excited.Stefon Diggs gets a special moment as a proud dadWhile Cardi's birthday tribute was filled with emotional words, Diggs also marked the occasion in his own way. The Washington Commanders wide receiver reportedly shared pictures with Grey on his Instagram Story, including a sweet father-and-son moment at an NFL stadium. He affectionately called his little boy "Gorditoooo."Grey is Diggs' first child with Cardi and his youngest addition to the family. Cardi also shares three children, Kulture, Wave and Blossom, with her estranged husband Offset.For Diggs, the birthday celebration comes during another busy NFL season. The veteran wide receiver joined the Washington Commanders in August 2026 after spending the previous season with the New England Patriots. He has continued to be part of Washington's offense, recording 30 receptions for 303 yards and five touchdowns through the team's first nine games.Cardi's emotional birthday message has fans smilingBeyond the adorable pictures and viral numbers, Cardi's birthday message offered a more personal look at what Grey means to her. The rapper admitted that her pregnancy came during one of the most uncertain and high-pressure periods of her life. However, having Grey with her throughout that time gave her extra strength."I was growing you inside of me and at the same time you were giving me life!" she wrote.She also added a sweet play on his name, saying that Grey had given a new meaning to what a Grey day feels like."You light up my life and every room with your smile your laugh and your precious spirit," Cardi added.Now, with his name and face finally out in the open, Grey has already managed to become an internet favorite. And while his dad continues to make plays for the Commanders, his little boy has managed to pull off a viral moment of his own, without even knowing it!Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Serious health problems....": Travis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce took drastic action at Florida home after an alarming discovery
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Donna Kelce found herself at the centre of an unexpected home renovation conversation.
articles.body: Earlier this year, Donna Kelce found herself at the centre of an unexpected home renovation conversation. The mother of NFL stars Travis and Jason Kelce decided to replace nine windows and six doors at her Florida property. While the project may sound like a routine household upgrade, her reason for doing so could strike a chord with homeowners dealing with rising energy bills, uncomfortable indoor temperatures and persistent moisture around their windows. Her decision also raises an important question: when does an ageing window become more than just an eyesore?Why Donna Kelce decided to replace her windowsTravis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce's decision came down to two practical concerns: controlling household expenses and dealing with condensation. Florida's humid climate can put considerable pressure on home interiors, particularly when older windows fail to provide proper insulation.Speaking on the New Heights podcast, she explained the reason behind the renovation, saying, “I’m doing something so that I can save money on heating and air conditioning and to keep my windows from sweating,” she added, “That’s as simple as it is.”The project was expected to take three days. However, the problem she described is not limited to Florida homes.Condensation, often called window sweating, occurs when moisture collects on glass surfaces. According to HVAC expert Richie Drew, this can point to excess indoor humidity and poor ventilation. He also warned that leaving moisture problems unresolved could encourage mould and bacteria to develop.“When windows are kept closed, and there’s insufficient air circulation inside, condensation can quickly form on the glass panes. If left unaddressed, this moisture can create serious problems for your health and home as mold, bacteria, and other toxins start to build up,” Drew explained.When should homeowners replace their windows?Donna Kelce's renovation also highlights when homeowners should consider making similar improvements. However, replacing every window is not always the right answer.Drew recommends arranging a professional energy audit before spending money on new windows or doors. An assessment can identify air leaks, insulation problems and inefficient heating or cooling systems. This helps homeowners understand where their energy is going and whether their windows are actually responsible.Older single-pane windows, metal frames and poorly sealed sliding windows can allow indoor air to escape. Replacing them with double- or triple-pane models featuring Low-E coatings can improve insulation and reduce energy waste.For those not ready for a major renovation, smaller improvements can also make a difference. Weatherstripping, window film, storm windows and insulated curtains can help limit drafts. Regular HVAC servicing is equally important, with Drew recommending professional maintenance twice a year.Ultimately, Donna Kelce's renovation offers a useful reminder: windows do more than brighten a room. They also influence indoor comfort, moisture levels and household expenses. Before investing in replacements, homeowners should identify the actual problem and choose an upgrade that addresses it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Grading the trade: Jaguars making run at Super Bowl after landing Eagles DT Jordan Davis
articles.summary: The Eagles signed Jordan Davis to a massive extension this offseason but couldn't pass up on the haul they got back for him.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars made their third trade on Monday, and it was the biggest one yet — literally and figuratively.

The Eagles will ship massive defensive tackle Jordan Davis (6-foot-6, 336 pounds) to the Jaguars . In return, Jacksonville will fork over a 2027 first-round draft pick and a 2029 second-round selection to Philadelphia.

Earlier Monday, the Jaguars acquired safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints.

How does Davis fit into the Jaguars' defense? What about the haul they got in return? Let's break down this massive trade.

If you thought the Bates trade was a sign that the Jaguars were going for it , the Davis trade left no doubt.

When DaVon Hamilton went down with a season-ending injury, it was viewed as a massive loss. Hamilton might not be a household name outside of Jacksonville, but he was valued highly inside the team's facility.

So what did the Jaguars do? They went out and got two defensive tackles to plug that hole — nearly 700 combined pounds between them. Think that will plug the hole up front?

The Jaguars might still have a top-10 rushing defense this season, but the Baltimore Ravens ran for a season-high 172 yards against them in their first game without Hamilton. That the game happened Thursday night likely allowed the Jaguars to recalibrate their needs over the weekend and strike quickly Monday. Three times, in fact.

They were not getting major interior help from the likes of Arik Armstead, Ruke Orhorhoro, Matt Dickerson and Albert Regis, and that's why the Jaguars added multiple players up front. The appeal of Godchaux is that he can play in multiple spots, and Davis also can move around a little, although they figure to hold down the nose between them. That likely leaves Armstead and Orhorhoro as the 3-techniques.

If you look at the Jaguars' remaining schedule, there aren't a lot of strong running teams left on it. However, if we're using the all-in framework, this deal was as much about what the Jaguars might face in the playoffs. Three of the top four teams by rush average reside in the AFC — the Pittsburgh Steelers, Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs — and the Jaguars might have to go through at least two of them to get to the Super Bowl.

Now comes the cost, and it's robust. Next year's first-round pick is likely to be in the bottom half of Round 1. The Jaguars hope it's the 32nd pick, which goes to the Super Bowl winner; if the season ended today, they'd be giving up the 25th overall selection . We can't project where the 2029 second-rounder will land, but teams often subtract one round for every year in the future, which makes it about a fourth-rounder for now.

When you put it like that, the cost doesn't sound quite as high, even if there are some conditions attached. Still, you have to appreciate a team willing and able to strike when the irons are hot.

The flip side: Davis has been ordinary this season — and at times invisible. The Jaguars clearly feel they can unlock his talent, or they wouldn't have paid so much. Lining up on a unit that features Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker should help, but Davis' paltry production (0.5 sacks, two QB hits, no forced fumbles or tackles for loss and a snap rate hovering around 50%) is concerning.

The Eagles signed Davis to a three-year, $78 million extension in March, yet Davis' salary cap hit for 2027 is a very reasonable figure at just over $8.5 million. This is an important element for the deal, with the Jaguars relatively tight against the projected cap for next spring. There's plenty of time to make it all work down the road.

For now, the Jaguars have their sights set on a Super Bowl.

Eagles couldn't pass on huge return for depreciating asset

The Eagles had let it be known that Moro Ojomo, the team's talented third-year defensive tackle, was not available for trade. And they kept to their word.

Instead, they dealt Davis, whom the team signed to a major extension along with Jalen Carter this offseason. The thinking was that Davis and Carter would be the starting pillars up front for years to come. That now has come to an end, but a Carter-Ojomo pairing now sounds appealing, especially with Davis performing at a disappointing level this season.

In addition to shedding salary, the Eagles also have continued adding to their impressive draft-pick nest egg. In 2027, they now own the Jaguars' first-rounder, the Vikings third-rounder, plus other teams' Day 3 picks, in addition to most of their own selections. In the 2028 draft, they own the Patriots' first-rounder and the Ravens' second-rounder. And now they're adding 2029 selections to the till.

With Jalen Hurts' career hanging in the balance following his blood clot diagnosis, the Eagles need that flexibility in case they must acquire another quarterback. That's the reality. Even if Hurts is eventually cleared to play, there's some long-term doubt about whether he remains the face of the franchise.

With the Eagles showing a willingness to deal assets, it appears that they're fully throwing in the towel on the playoffs, even with the NFC East nominally still up for grabs. That also impacts Nick Sirianni's future as he now coaches a team that has gone from possible Super Bowl contenders to more talent-poor in a hurry, especially given all their injury trouble.

It's a tough short-term pill to swallow for the franchise and a fan base used to competing every season, but the long-term payoff could be immense. The Eagles' to-do list this offseason grows, but the potential of how they can reshape the roster is equally as exciting.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $200 million Six Flags investment faces $279 dining pass lawsuit as frustrated customers demand long-overdue refunds
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has helped Six Flags attract attention with his star power and financial backing.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has helped Six Flags attract attention with his star power and financial backing. However, the amusement park giant is now facing an uncomfortable situation as customers demand answers over money they say they are still owed. A new class-action lawsuit involving Six Flags and Enchanted Parks has brought the company's customer service problems into focus. The dispute centres on dining plans that became invalid after a change in park ownership, leaving families waiting months for refunds. With Kelce connected to the company as both an investor and brand ambassador, the controversy adds another layer of interest.Travis Kelce's Six Flags connection draws attention amid refund controversyTravis Kelce's relationship with Six Flags goes beyond a promotional partnership. In October 2025, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end joined investment firm Jana Partners and other business executives in an investment group that acquired a collective economic interest of approximately 9% in Six Flags Entertainment. The group wanted to encourage changes that could improve the company's value and guest experience.The following March, Six Flags announced Kelce as its brand ambassador for 2026. His role included supporting marketing campaigns, creating digital content and promoting the company's amusement parks across North America.The partnership made sense given Kelce's childhood connection to amusement parks. However, the latest lawsuit puts the company's guest experience under a different kind of spotlight.The dispute began after Enchanted Parks acquired Six Flags St. Louis in April 2026. The new operator announced that previously purchased dining plans would no longer be accepted. Customers could request refunds or choose an alternative, but several reportedly struggled to receive their money.Six Flags and Enchanted Parks face class-action lawsuit over refundsOne customer, Sonya Parrent, has now taken legal action alongside her attorney, Christopher Roberts. Parrent paid $279 for dining plans for her family and said she had been waiting six months for a refund.She recalled receiving a message promising payment within three to five business days in August. However, the money never arrived.Roberts believes thousands of customers may have faced similar problems. He explained, “What happened is that Sonya, and we believe thousands of customers, kind of got left behind. They purchased these meal plans, which are actually significantly more expensive than the season passes, and they didn’t get anything in return,”The attorney also questioned why customers had to choose between a refund and a gift card within a limited period. He believes all affected dining plan holders deserve their money back, along with interest.Six Flags acknowledged the frustration and said most eligible refunds had been processed. Its statement added:“We recognize the frustration of Enchanted Parks guests who submitted Dining Plan refund requests and appreciate their continued patience. Most eligible refunds have been processed, and we are committed to working through individual cases where the original refund attempt was unsuccessful.”Enchanted Parks had not responded to First Alert 4's request for comment at the time of publication.Meanwhile, Parrent remains unhappy with the company's response. She said Enchanted Parks offered her a discount on a season pass for next year, but questioned the offer while her refund remained unresolved.“Now you want me to spend more money with you, and you haven’t even given me a refund,” responded Parrent.For Six Flags, the lawsuit raises questions about how the ownership transition was handled. With Kelce serving as a prominent face of the brand and part of its investor group, the company's ability to restore customer confidence could become an important part of its next chapter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2018, Josh Allen bought a $660,000 Buffalo-area home; 5 years later, he added a $7.2 million California retreat
articles.summary: Josh Allen paid $659,900 for a house in Orchard Park, New York, in 2018, soon after the Buffalo Bills drafted him.
articles.body: Josh Allen paid $659,900 for a house in Orchard Park, New York, in 2018, soon after the Buffalo Bills drafted him. In July 2023, he closed on a $7.2 million beach home in Dana Point, California. The gap between those price tags is huge, but the story is bigger than money. It shows how a quarterback raised on a farm chose to spend his first big paychecks, and why his main base still sits five minutes from the stadium. Both buys were deliberate, and each says something different about him.How Josh Allen went from a $660,000 Buffalo home to a $7.2 million California retreatAllen bought the Orchard Park house for $659,900 in 2018, the year Buffalo picked him in the first round out of Wyoming. Reports put it at about 3,600 square feet, with a pool in the backyard. His rookie contract was worth roughly $21 million, fully guaranteed over four years, so he could have shopped far higher. He did not. That choice says plenty about him before you even get to the California deal.The second purchase closed on July 5, 2023. The home is a single-story, 2,808-square-foot place in Monarch Bay, a guard-gated community in Dana Point, roughly 60 miles south of Los Angeles. The asking price was $7.5 million, and Allen paid $7.2 million. It has four bedrooms and three bathrooms, and the neighborhood comes with access to a beach club. His six-year, $258 million extension, signed in 2021, began with the 2023 season, so the money was there.The comparison is a little unfair, of course. One house belonged to a rookie who had not thrown an NFL pass. The other belongs to a proven star on one of the richest contracts in football. Still, five years of change fit neatly between those two price tags.Why a franchise quarterback kept living in a modest Orchard Park houseMoney was never the obstacle. Allen could have moved into a mansion years ago. Instead, he doubled down on the same corner of Western New York. In 2021, he bought 31 acres in Orchard Park for $500,000 through an LLC, according to Realtor.com. Added to his existing property, that gives him a compound of roughly 46 acres, with a pool house and a sports court. The land sits about eight minutes from Highmark Stadium.Sports Illustrated has called his Buffalo home shockingly cheap for a player at his level, and one report now values it above $1 million. That is still a rounding error next to his income.My read is simple. Western New York is one of the few NFL markets where a quarterback can buy space and privacy without paying a premium for either. A star in Los Angeles or Miami pays for the address. In Buffalo, Allen pays for dirt, and dirt appears to be what he wants. He grew up on a family farm near Firebaugh, California, on ground his family has worked since his great-grandfather arrived from Sweden in 1907. Open acreage probably feels like home to him.What the Dana Point house gives him that Buffalo cannotWeather is the obvious answer, but it is not the whole one. Allen spends the season in a city where winter shows up early and leaves late. Dana Point gives him an offseason base in his home state, with the ocean, quiet streets and an exclusive golf club nearby. He plays golf as a hobby, so that detail fits.There is a football angle too. The Monarch Beach area has been home to Sam Darnold and former NFL quarterback Mark Sanchez, and Allen is a known friend of Darnold. A gated street full of people who understand the job is worth something when the season ends and the noise does not.Timing adds another layer. Allen bought the house shortly after he began dating actress Hailee Steinfeld in May 2023, according to multiple reports. Whether the two events are connected is guesswork. What is clear is that he wanted a place that was his, away from the football calendar, and that he could pay for it without stretching.Buffalo is where he works. Dana Point is where he rests. Splitting life that way is common among players with long careers ahead of them, and it keeps both places from feeling like the same place.Why Josh Allen listed the California house for $8.5 million after his weddingAllen and Steinfeld married in late May 2025 in Montecito, California. Within weeks, Realtor.com showed the Dana Point house on the market at $8.5 million. That is $1.3 million above what he paid, although an asking price is not a sale price. Sports Illustrated labeled it a bachelor pad he no longer needed, and the timing supports that reading.Steinfeld has her own property. Reports say she bought a 9,000-square-foot home in Encino in 2021 for $7.975 million, and that it once belonged to John Fogerty. Two people with homes of that size and a shared life do not need a third house that was bought for one of them.Cash was not the driver either. Allen signed a new six-year, $330 million extension with Buffalo in 2025, which makes the listing a lifestyle decision, not a financial one. One September 2026 report says the house returned to the market, so check current listings before treating any sale as settled.What stays constant is Orchard Park. The house he bought for $659,900 and the land he added in 2021 remain his anchor, no matter where the beach home ends up.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Travis Kelce's $5.35 million Ohio mansion gets unexpected neighborhood support amid growing privacy fence controversy
articles.summary: Travis Kelce may have found a few unexpected allies in the growing dispute over his $5.35 million Ohio mansion.
articles.body: Travis Kelce may have found a few unexpected allies in the growing dispute over his $5.35 million Ohio mansion. While some Bratenahl residents have raised objections to the property's renovation and landscaping plans, not everyone in the lakeside community shares their concerns. One local homeowner has now spoken out in support of the Kansas City Chiefs star and his famous partner, pushing back against claims that the couple faces widespread opposition. With another community meeting approaching, the latest comments offer a different picture of the neighborhood tensions surrounding their new home.Travis Kelce receives neighborhood support amid Ohio mansion disputeThe debate surrounding Kelce's Bratenahl property has attracted considerable attention, particularly over plans for a six-foot black aluminium privacy fence and changes to the surrounding landscape.However, a resident who lives minutes from the property told Page Six that the negative reaction does not represent the entire village.“I think they’re excited. I think it’s great,” a neighbor who lives minutes from the property told Page Six exclusively. “I don’t think people are angry.”The resident believes most of the objections come from homeowners living directly beside the property rather than the wider community.“I think it’s just the neighbors on either side who object. I don’t know why they object — they’ve done a really nice job fixing up the house.”The neighbor also wants Kelce and Taylor Swift to feel comfortable in their new surroundings. They even contacted other residents ahead of the November 10 Architectural Review Board meeting to encourage a welcoming atmosphere.“We don’t want them to feel unwelcome,” they explained, adding that “the rest of the neighborhood will absolutely be supportive. Everyone else has been excited.”Bratenahl has around 1,200 residents, making the disagreement particularly noticeable in the small lakeside community.Travis Kelce's $5.35 million mansion faces fresh landscaping objectionsDespite the support, several homeowners remain concerned about the proposed changes. Their objections include the removal of trees and shrubs, the potential impact of the fence on local deer and landscaping work near existing infrastructure.One major concern involves a century-old shared sewer line. Neighbor Katherine Bolton has warned that planting evergreen trees nearby could create serious problems because of their roots. She reportedly received a $75,000 estimate to protect the pipe.Kelce and Swift's planner, Jacob Kutz of Tiny Construction, has defended the plans, explaining that the couple wants privacy and security following one of the largest property sales in Cuyahoga County.The original proposal included an eight-foot fence, but the plans were later reduced to six feet, with the structure stopping short of Lake Erie.The couple have not attended the previous community meetings in person, instead relying on representatives to present their plans.For now, the disagreement remains unresolved. However, the latest support from a local resident suggests that the couple may have more welcoming neighbors than the controversy initially indicated.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes, two of the strongest players in the Kansas City Chiefs, have grown pretty close to one another in the last few years.
articles.body: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes, two of the strongest players in the Kansas City Chiefs, have grown pretty close to one another in the last few years. This has also led the two to launch their own venture, a highly rated steakhouse, 1587 Prime. But the restaurant has found itself in a mess after it was sued by a sneaker company. Amid this, there has been an update about the steakhouse.Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes’ 1587 Prime makes an announcement amid the legal mess and copyright issuesA few days ago, Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes’ 1587 Prime announced its new Thanksgiving menu along with their new operating hours.According to reports, on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, the popular steakhouse 1587 Prime will run its operations from 2 p.m. to 8 p.m.The special menu will consist of a lobster bisque for $22, 160z Prime Rob for $80, stuffed Turkey Roulade for $55 per person, pumpkin cake for $18, Gather & Give Cocktail for $19.The announcement of the new Thanksgiving menu has sparked excitement among many as fans look forward to visiting the 1587 Prime steakhouse amid the legal mess it has found itself in.Why were Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes sued over starting 1587 Prime?For the unversed, Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes’ 1587 Prime was sued by a sneaker company earlier this year over copyright infringement.1587 Sneakers, a footwear and apparel company, filed a federal trademark infringement lawsuit against Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, alongside their hospitality partner Noble 33, over the name of their luxury steakhouse, 1587 Prime.But things took a turn when both the Kansas City Chiefs’ star players Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce maintained distance from the mess as their teams claimed in court that the two are not actively engaged in the business.1587 Sneakers did not agree to this version as a court filing read as, "Defendants Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes seek dismissal by recasting themselves as two distant celebrities that are mere promotional 'pretty faces' of the alleged infringing enterprise with no New York ties…”The filing added, “The record shows otherwise. "As sufficiently alleged in the operative complaint, both Defendants played an active personal role as the 'moving forces' of the at-issue mark as '1587' was approved and constructed from their respective football jersey numbers: 15 and 87."Neither the quarterback Patrick Mahomes nor the top tight end Travis Kelce has addressed the issue in public as both of them have remained focused on their careers and have remained committed to their team, the Kansas City Chiefs.For now, all eyes remain on them as the team has made an impressive comeback.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Did Sean McVay make the wrong call? Puka Nacua’s injury leaves Los Angeles Rams coach regretting decision
articles.summary: Sean McVay has a reason to question his final offensive call against the Washington Commanders.
articles.body: Sean McVay has a reason to question his final offensive call against the Washington Commanders. The Los Angeles Rams won 20-13 on November 8, 2026, but Puka Nacua left the game with a right knee injury after taking a hard hit on a late jet sweep. The Rams coach later admitted he was unhappy with the decision. His concern was not just the injury itself, but whether he could have chosen a safer way to close out the game.The play came on third-and-11, with Los Angeles trying to keep possession and run down the clock. Instead, Nacua took the ball and gained five yards before Jeremy Reaves and Sonny Styles stopped him. The receiver stayed on the ground in pain before teammates helped him up. McVay took responsibility for the call and questioned whether another play could have secured the conversion without exposing his leading receiver to that hit. Sean McVay questions his final play call after Puka Nacua takes a hard hitMcVay did not hide his frustration when reporters asked about the decision in a recent interview. Speaking during his press conference, the Rams head coach admitted he had replayed the moment in his head several times."I'm kicking myself about those kinds of things," McVay said. "I'd be lying to you if I said I haven't questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head."He also wondered if another play could have helped Los Angeles get the first down and end the game without putting Nacua in that position. McVay said he felt "tremendous responsibility" for the decision and stressed that the Rams must find ways to protect their players while still using their abilities to help the team.There was a reason the call caught his attention. Nacua had already done more than enough on offense. He finished the game with 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown on 19 targets. He also added 20 rushing yards on two carries. His final touch, however, came on the play that left him injured.The Rams still got the result they wanted, but the final offensive sequence gave McVay something very different to think about.Puka Nacua's knee injury could keep him out for at least four gamesThe injury turned out to be more serious than an initial sideline scare. Recently, McVay revealed that Nacua had suffered sprains to his medial collateral ligament (MCL) and posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) in his right knee, along with turf toe. The coach also said the receiver would likely land on injured reserve.An IR move would keep Nacua out for at least four games. That is a major setback for a Rams offense that has already lost another important receiver.Davante Adams remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. His absence had already put more responsibility on Nacua, who led the Rams' receiving group against Washington. Now Matthew Stafford could have to work with a much thinner group of wideouts.Nacua has recorded 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns in seven games this season. His 150-yard performance against Washington was his best receiving game of the campaign. He also helped the Rams secure their third straight win, taking their record to 5-4.McVay also expressed sympathy for his receiver during Monday's press conference. He said he was disappointed to see Nacua and other players dealing with injuries, but the team would have to adjust and move forward.That leaves the Rams with two problems to solve. They need to find a way to replace Nacua's production, and they need to be more careful with how they use their remaining offensive weapons.McVay cannot change the decision he made against Washington. However, his own words show that he has already started questioning it. The Rams got the win, but losing their leading receiver on a play designed to help close out the game is a price the coach clearly wishes they had not paid.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Josh Allen's end-zone throw turns into a stunning disaster as Troy Aikman amazed by Byron Murphy Jr.'s Vikings heroics
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings cornerback Byron Murphy Jr. gave Troy Aikman a moment he will not forget anytime soon.
articles.body: Minnesota Vikings cornerback Byron Murphy Jr. gave Troy Aikman a moment he will not forget anytime soon. Murphy pulled off an incredible interception against Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen on Monday night, leaving the veteran NFL analyst amazed. The cornerback raced across the field, got in front of wide receiver DJ Moore and picked off Allen's pass in the end zone. He then turned the interception into a 55-yard return, making an already impressive defensive play even better.The moment came during the Vikings' Week 9 matchup against the Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9, 2026. Allen looked ready to connect with Moore for a touchdown, but Murphy had other ideas. His speed and awareness helped him reach the ball before the receiver could make the catch. Even Aikman, who has seen some of the biggest moments in NFL history, struggled to hide his excitement.Why Troy Aikman was amazed by Byron Murphy Jr.'s incredible interceptionAllen had a promising opportunity to find Moore in the end zone. The Bills quarterback has the arm strength to make difficult throws look routine, and the pass appeared to give his receiver a chance to score. However, Murphy refused to let the play develop as Allen expected.The Vikings cornerback read the throw and immediately sprinted towards the ball. Moore had a chance to make the catch, but Murphy reached the spot first and secured the interception. He then stayed on his feet and ran the ball back 55 yards, giving Minnesota a huge defensive moment.Aikman could not hold back his reaction during ESPN's Monday Night Football broadcast on November 9. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback described Murphy's effort as "one of the best plays I've ever seen."That was a remarkable compliment from a three-time Super Bowl champion who spent years competing at the highest level. His broadcast partner Joe Buck also had a brief but telling reaction. He simply said, "wow," as the replay showed Murphy's incredible run towards the ball.The interception stood out because Murphy did more than just get into position. He had to cover significant ground, beat Moore to the football and then turn the play into a long return. It was a terrific individual effort against one of the NFL's most dangerous quarterbacks.Byron Murphy's big play adds to the Vikings' defensive statement against Josh AllenThe interception also highlighted the challenge facing Allen against Minnesota's defense. Both teams entered the November 9 matchup with 6-1 records, making it an important meeting between two teams with strong Super Bowl ambitions.Allen has built his reputation on his ability to stretch the field and make plays under pressure. His arm strength often allows him to target receivers even when defenders seem to have an advantage. However, Murphy showed that even a quarterback like Allen can pay for a moment of misjudgment.The Vikings cornerback's recovery speed made the difference. Moore initially looked like he had a chance to reach the pass, but Murphy never gave up on the play. He chased the football, got in front of the receiver and changed possession in a matter of seconds.For Minnesota, the interception offered more than a highlight for the Monday night broadcast. It showed how quickly the defense could turn a potential Bills touchdown into an opportunity for the Vikings. Murphy's 55-yard return made the play even more memorable.Aikman's reaction captured the moment perfectly. He has watched countless NFL games throughout his playing and broadcasting career, yet Murphy's effort earned a rare compliment. Against Josh Allen and the Bills, the Vikings cornerback produced a play that even a Super Bowl-winning quarterback could hardly believe.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: It’s Monday Night Football on ESPN, and therefore it’s time for the NFL world to do its weekly check-in on the drama between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck. It’s n...
articles.body:
It's Monday Night Football on ESPN, and therefore it's time for the NFL world to do its weekly check-in on the drama between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck.

It's no secret anymore that the two reportedly have issues with each other now that ESPN has given Buck a new contract, and Aikman isn't likely to remain with the company after the Super Bowl.

Fans Call Out Noticeable Tension Between Joe Buck and Troy Aikman Amid Rift

Buck and Aikman are still chugging along to finish out the season despite not being on the same page anymore. Despite calling six Super Bowls together, their relationship has hit a breaking point, and fans are starting to see more signs of it on Week 9's Monday Night Football broadcast.

"The tension between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck is hard to miss. One of the most uncomfortable broadcasts to watch," said one fan .

"There is no fluidity; they aren't even trying to hide it," added a user on X .

Aikman and Buck still have plenty of games left together before either can think about moving on, but the uncertainty comes at an awkward time for ESPN. The network is preparing to broadcast its first Super Bowl, the biggest event in its history, and would have preferred to enter that moment with its lead booth firmly settled.

An extension for Aikman could have eliminated the uncertainty, but the situation now appears to have deteriorated to the point where repairing the relationship may be difficult.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

"It's awkward listening to Joe Buck just talk forever because Aikman is trying to prove a point," said one fan .

"Watching Joe Buck and Troy Aikman with no sound, knowing that they hate each other, is peak," wrote another fan .

There was one moment during the pregame that caught fans' attention: Aikman smiling, while Buck was not with him.

While the beef between them was initially just a rumor, it has become much more apparent with each passing week. ESPN will hope the two can keep it professional until the Super Bowl, as they don't want to scramble for a replacement before the big game.

"Look how happy Troy Aikman is when he's not around Joe Buck," said one fan .

"Bruh, Troy Aikman HATES Joe Buck," another fan chimed in .

Aikman and Buck haven't exactly been handed an offensive showcase in Monday night's Minnesota Vikings-Buffalo Bills matchup.

Buffalo leads 10-6 at halftime, with defense dictating the game so far. The Bills have done enough to keep Minnesota's struggling offense in check, while the Vikings' defense has made life difficult for one of the league's No. 1-ranked offenses on PFN's Offense Impact Metric.

It has been a grind on the field, and apparently there is another battle unfolding off it.

articles.title: Browns HC 'really proud' of Shedeur Sanders' play in Week 9
articles.summary: Todd Monken liked what he saw from his young quarterback in Week 9.
articles.body:
Winning in the NFL with a backup quarterback isn't easy. Especially when you average less than 3.0 yards per carry on the ground. However, the Cleveland Browns almost did exactly that today.

Shedeur Sanders got the start for an injured Deshaun Watson. And although his performance wasn't as good as the box score may indicate, he also didn't play them out of this game. His pair of passing touchdowns in the final 20:00 minutes of play gave the team a chance to win.

Head coach Todd Monken had this to say about the young quarterback's effort.

Forget the nearly 300 passing yards you'll see in the box score. That was mostly the result of three plays where the wide receiver made things happen that had nothing to do with the quarterback.

We should all take this praise from Monken at face value. Backup quarterbacks have to work hard to stay ready in the NFL. Sanders was able to do that, and it's worth shining a light on since we don't see the day-to-day grind that he puts in.

Does this mean that Sanders should take over as the starter? Of course not. But it's a credit to his professionalism as a young player.

Sunday was a disappointing day for the Cleveland Browns . They lost in overtime to the New Orleans Saints and began to fall further behind in the race for the AFC North. However, there was some silver lining in this game.

Rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion scored his first career touchdown in the NFL. Overall, he tallied 85 receiving yards and the one score in this game. He had this to say on finally reaching the end zone.

It truly was a highlight catch worthy of being his first. Not only did he get open, but he had to come back for the ball, make a more difficult catch, and rack up nearly 30 by cutting back across the field. Not only that, but it gave the Browns the lead with just over five minutes to go in the fourth quarter.

Concepcion was one of the Browns' two first-round picks in the 2026 NFL draft. After his first 100+ yard receiving game two weeks ago and now finally finding the end zone, it's starting to feel like the rookie is finding his footing in the NFL.
