The Buffalo Bills joined the San Francisco 49ers ay 7-1 with their Monday night win over the Minnesota Vikings.

Buffalo and San Francisco sit on top of their respective conferences going into Week 10.

The Vikings entered Monday as the No. 2 seed in the NFC, but after the loss to the Bills, they are now the third-best team in the NFC North.

All three of the NFC's wild-card positions are held by NFC North franchises. Minnesota's playoff spot could be in big-time danger, though, if it doesn't find an answer at quarterback.

Buffalo maintained its position atop the AFC with its double-digit win in Minnesota.

The Bills are three games ahead of the New England Patriots in the loss column in the AFC East.

There's still half of a season to play, but the Bills are trending in the right direction to cruise to the divisional crown.

The Bills should head to Kansas City on Thanksgiving with a 9-1 mark since they play the Miami Dolphins and New York Jets in the next two weeks.

The challenging part of Buffalo's schedule begins on Thanksgiving. It also faces the Denver Broncos on Christmas Day as well as visits the Denver Broncos and Green Bay Packers in consecutive weeks to start December.

The primary focus in the AFC in Week 10 will be the AFC North, where the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals face each other on Sunday night. The winner of that game will be in sole possession of first place.

Minnesota went from first to third in the NFC North with its loss to Buffalo.

The Vikings are down to the No. 6 seed just two weeks after they were the NFL's last unbeaten team.

Kevin O'Connell's team has a tremendous defense, but it struggled once again on offense with Carson Wentz at the helm.

The Vikings must figure out their quarterback situation to have a shot at keeping their place inside the NFC's top seven teams.

The Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams are lurking in eighth and ninth places are potential replacements for the Vikings in the wild-card slots.

Minnesota plays Green Bay and San Francisco in the next two weeks, so there's a decent chance it falls out of the top seven, especially if nothing changes at quarterback.

Green Bay has a lot to gain from its Week 10 home clash with the Vikings. It could move within a half-game of the Chicago Bears, who are off next week, with a win.

articles.title: Bills Beat Vikings, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Allen, Wentz, Cook, Jefferson, Top Players
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills have looked like Super Bowl contenders through the first half of the season, and they did little to dispel that notion on Monday.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have looked like Super Bowl contenders through the first half of the season, and they did little to dispel that notion on Monday.

The Bills trounced the Minnesota Vikings 23-6 in what was their best defensive performance of the year so far.

Carson Wentz was filling in for the injured Kyler Murray on Monday, but he didn't do much to claim the starting job from him, to say the least.

It wasn't the most impressive night from Josh Allen and the Bills' offense, but it was enough to get the job done against a Vikings offense that put up a laughable performance.

Both teams had a slow start to the game, starting off with a punt from each side, followed by an interception from Allen and a backwards pass that resulted in a fumble from the Vikings.

Buffalo got on the board with a field goal in the first quarter, but six straight punts followed to continue the quiet start from both teams.

The Vikings nearly got the ball on the Bills' goal line when they sacked Allen and forced a fumble, but he was ruled down before the ball came out.

Minnesota tied things up with a field goal in the second quarter, but the Bills answered on the following drive when Allen found a wide-open Keleki Latu in the end zone. The Vikings hit another field goal to cut the deficit to four heading into halftime.

If the Vikings' offense was bad in the first half, it was horrific in the second half.

Wentz opened up the third quarter with an interception that set up a Bills field goal. On the following drive, he threw his second interception of the game.

Running back James Cook III found the end zone halfway through the fourth quarter to make it a 20-6 Buffalo lead, and a field goal on the Bills' next drive just about sealed the win.

With just over four minutes remaining, the Vikings turned to Max Brosmer under center, and he gave them a little bit of life late for a moment in the game. Ultimately, he didn't have enough to inspire an improbable comeback.

articles.title: Vikings Will 'Explore Their Options' At QB Before Trade Deadline, NFL Insider Says amid Cousins Buzz
articles.summary: Perhaps the biggest thing holding the Minnesota Vikings back from being Super Bowl contenders is their quarterback room, and they might be looking to upgrade ahead of the trade deadline.
articles.body:
Perhaps the biggest thing holding the Minnesota Vikings back from being Super Bowl contenders is their quarterback room, and they might be looking to upgrade ahead of the trade deadline.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday that the Vikings are "definitely gonna explore their options," citing Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones and Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins as two players they might check in on.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell offered little insight into whether the Minnesota will try to acquire a quarterback before the deadline.

The Vikings' quarterback room currently consists of Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer, though Murray is currently week-to-week with a hamstring strain.

Wentz got the start on Monday against the Buffalo Bills and struggled tremendously, throwing for just 81 yards on 8-of-25 passing, along with two interceptions and a fumble in the 23-6 loss. Brosmer came in late and completed six of his seven passes for 58 yards.

Landing a starting-caliber quarterback in the middle of the season might be a tough task for the Vikings, but Indianapolis perhaps is the place to start. The Colts are conducting a fire sale amid a 2-7 start and have already traded a number of key players.

Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported on Sunday, however, that Indianapolis won't be trading Jones ahead of the deadline, so the Vikings would need to make quite the offer to get the Colts to change their minds.

Jones hasn't matched his success from last season, throwing for 1,722 yards, six touchdowns and 10 interceptions so far, but it's still fair to say that he'd be an upgrade to the Vikings' offense.

The Raiders seem to be taking a similar approach to their quarterback situation, as multiple reports have indicated that they're not interested in dealing Cousins.

Despite Las Vegas' struggles, Cousins has put together a solid season with 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Unfortunately for the Vikings, a reunion might not be in the cards.

Minnesota has a Super Bowl-caliber defense, but likely can't win it all with any of its current quarterbacks. Whether the Vikings will be able to find a new quarterback in the coming hours remains to be seen, but now is certainly the time to go all out in search of a signal-caller.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 10: After some massive trades, the Jaguars take the top spot
articles.summary: The Jaguars might have won the trade deadline with a flurry of moves.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

The Jaguars were the quietest team in the NFL this past offseason.

It was odd. They were coming off a 13-4 season and general manager James Gladstone had let everyone know he would be aggressive. The Travis Hunter trade in 2025 and his comments afterward — "I know every step that I didn't take that related to fear, I regretted," he said — set a foundation for his approach. Then, in the offseason, nobody spent less money than the Jaguars in free agency, and they didn't have a first-round draft pick.

Apparently, Gladstone saw a market inefficiency in the pre-deadline trade market, and was waiting to spring his plan on everyone.

The Jaguars could look around the NFL and see there was no definitive Super Bowl favorite. So they decided to become one. Jacksonville made a series of trades Monday to get safety Jessie Bates III, and defensive tackles Davon Godchaux and Jordan Davis before Tuesday's deadline . The Jaguars were the No. 1 team in DVOA and led the NFL in point differential before those trades. Now they're much, much better.

Godchaux and Davis replace DaVon Hamilton, the excellent defensive tackle who was the key driver in the Jaguars having the top run defense in football before he suffered a season-ending quad injury in Week 8. Bates gives Jacksonville an excellent playmaker on the back end. That goes with an offense that is fourth in the NFL in points scored, fifth in EPA ( expected points added ) per play and sixth in DVOA.

The Jaguars gave up a lot. They sent off a 2027 first-round pick and two second-round picks in the deals. And nobody in Jacksonville will care about the draft picks if this ends in a Super Bowl. And it might. That's why Jacksonville takes over the top spot in the power rankings. The Jaguars already looked like a Super Bowl contender before the trades. Now they look like the favorite. After three decades of waiting to make a Super Bowl, the Jaguars are pushing hard to get the job done this season.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 9:

1. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, Last week: 3)

It has already been a year for unexpected champions. Indiana, one of the worst power conference programs in college football history, won the national title with an undefeated season. Michigan men's basketball won a title for the first time since 1989. The New York Knicks won the NBA championship, their first since 1973. The Milwaukee Brewers won their first World Series in their 57th season.

The Jaguars saw that and wanted to join the fun. They are one of four franchises, along with the Lions, Browns and Texans, to never make a Super Bowl. But the Jaguars saw an opportunity and pushed a lot of chips in on trades to upgrade the defense . They also have the third-easiest remaining schedule, according to DVOA, giving them a good shot at the top seed in the AFC. Pulling off what the Hoosiers, Wolverines, Knicks and Brewers did in 2026 and giving their fans a celebration for a lifetime is now realistically on the table.

The 49ers didn't do anything to fall out of the top spot. The Jaguars' moves just gave them precedence, for now. The 49ers continued to look fantastic in Week 9, forcing five second-half turnovers by the Raiders. Their defense has been a major surprise and the Niners should continue to be good now that Nick Bosa is back in the lineup and DeForest Buckner is aboard via a trade .

Last season, Kyle Shanahan was a great NFL Coach of the Year candidate but was overlooked because that award often goes to coaches in their first year on the job and to coaches on teams that outperform preseason expectations. But for a second straight season the 49ers are winning despite major injuries. The job Shanahan has done with the 49ers should not be ignored again.

It's fair to look at Buffalo's last two opponents and be skeptical of the Bills' defensive hot streak, but there has been improvement. The Bills allowed 144 yards and 10 points to the Ravens two weeks ago, and 178 yards and six points against Minnesota on Monday night . That came against Joe Fagnano and Carson Wentz, but it's still two dominant performances in a row. For a defense that had been near the bottom of the league before that, it's at least possible that Buffalo is figuring some things out on that side of the ball. That would help them in an increasingly challenging AFC. With other AFC contenders making moves, most notably the Jaguars, it will be interesting to see what the Bills do to improve before the deadline.

The Bears still got to 27 points and did enough to beat the Buccaneers on Sunday night, but it was startling to see Chicago struggle as much as it did . After scoring touchdowns on their first two drives, the Bears' next 10 possessions were: four interceptions, a fumble, four punts and a field goal. Winning with that type of slump is notable. The Bears came up with the one play they needed, a 38-yard pass to a wide-open Colston Loveland, to get the game-winning field goal.

It was particularly strange to see Caleb Williams throw four interceptions, considering he had never thrown more than two in an NFL game. But he never lost confidence, which allowed him to hit Loveland when the Bears needed it. "I'll never not throw the ball," Williams said. "I could throw 100 picks in one game. If it comes down to it, I'm going to throw that pass that I threw to Colston, or if it's a tighter window, I'm going to rip it in there."

The Bengals had an odd game Sunday. They were torching the Falcons in the first half and then were content to take the air out of the ball in the second half. They had just 26 offensive plays in the second half and 19 of those came with them leading by at least 14 points. That's how Joe Burrow had just seven attempts and 32 passing yards after going 18 of 22 for 239 yards in the first half.

Volume was a hang-up for Burrow in the second half Sunday, but efficiency hasn't been an issue. He is completing 74% of his passes and has a shot to challenge Drew Brees' single-season completion record of 74.4%. His completion percentage over expectation (CPOE), a metric that measures a quarterback's accuracy, is a league-best 9.7, which is 3 points better than anyone else, according to RBSDM.com . Burrow is having a special season and will be in the MVP conversation until the end.

The most promising part of the Chiefs' win on Sunday against the Jets might be that Chris Jones and George Karlaftis each had two sacks. Karlaftis had two sacks for the season before Sunday, Jones had just half of a sack, and that's a big reason the Chiefs' pass rush ranked near the bottom of the league. Even with five sacks as a team Sunday, Kansas City still has just 14 sacks. That's the fourth-lowest mark in the NFL.

The Chiefs have been doing fine on defense without much of a pass rush, ranking top 10 in yards and points allowed. But it's hard to be a top-10 defense while ranking in the bottom five in sacks. Perhaps the performance against the Jets will get the pass rush going, and in turn boost a defense that has already played well.

The coin flipped on the Broncos' side again, as they won an NFL-record 16th straight one-score regular-season game. They have 22 wins, counting postseason, since the start of last season and an astonishing 18 of them have been by one score. The Broncos had fewer yards and first downs than the Panthers but won 26-21.

After seeing it happen so often, the Broncos believe this is not luck.

"Well, when it keeps happening, I think our league is what it is," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said, according to the team's transcripts. "When those things keep falling your way, that's not by accident."

One thing working in Denver's favor is its schedule. DVOA says the Broncos have the second-easiest remaining schedule, while AFC West rival Kansas City is the sixth-toughest.

Whatever was happening the first three weeks of the season with the Packers, they're far beyond that. Green Bay is 5-1 since a slow start. Since Week 4 it is fifth in EPA per play on offense and third in EPA per play allowed on defense. The Packers take a jump in the rankings for two reasons: The offense looked great again against the Patriots on Sunday, and Micah Parsons' return is looming for the defense. It is very easy to forget that when Parsons tore his ACL last season the Packers were 9-3-1 and leading in the second half at Denver. And Green Bay has been playing much better on defense the past six games.

Josh Jacobs' broken finger could have a negative effect. He will have finger surgery and miss a maximum of three weeks, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz . The Packers' running game has been horrible all season but a little better with Jacobs. Taking a step back in the run game could also affect the passing game, which has been cooking with Jordan Love turning Matthew Golden and Christian Watson into one of the NFL's top receiving duos.

Is the Lions' defense good? It has been better recently. For the third straight game the Lions' opponent failed to top 17 points. Two of those games happened against the offensively challenged Vikings and Dolphins; the third game in that streak was against the Packers. Advanced metrics are kind to the Lions' defense over the past three weeks too, as Detroit is eighth in EPA per play allowed and fifth in success rate allowed. Star safety Brian Branch returned from an Achilles injury three games ago, and it's not a coincidence the Lions' defense is much better with him back. The Lions have held opponents to 21 or fewer points in four straight games, the first time that has happened since 2016, according to the team's site .

The Lions allowed just 228 yards and 12 first downs Sunday, and while that was against Miami, it's still a lot better than Detroit looked on defense early in the season.

"We've cleaned a lot up," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said, via the team's site. "Guys are trusting what they're being taught, they're executing it and with that execution comes confidence."

Having a reliable backup quarterback in Drew Lock allows the Seahawks to take their time on Sam Darnold's return from a quad injury. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald told Seattle Sports 710AM that Seattle plans to start Lock again to give Darnold another week to heal. Lock filled in for Darnold on Sunday and was fine in a 17-3 win over the Cardinals. He didn't turn the ball over and didn't take a sack, which is a big key for any Seattle quarterback as long as the defense is playing as it usually does. Lock has thrown 76 passes this season without an interception.

"I know that's a big thing for me going into every week," Lock said, via The Athletic . "Knowing that we can control the game with the run, operate on third downs well, keep the ball in our hands."

Lock suffered an oblique injury Sunday but the Seahawks believe he'll be fine for their next game against the Raiders.

It's hard to remember the last time a team that was 6-2 with one of the top two defenses in the NFL felt this hopeless. Monday night's performance was absolutely deflating for the Vikings. Carson Wentz took over for an injured Kyler Murray, who had been struggling so much that everyone wondered if him sitting out Monday was a "soft benching." Then Wentz went 8 of 25 for 81 yards, two interceptions and an 8.9 passer rating. It was one of the worst quarterback performances in recent memory. For the second straight season, the Vikings cannot find one quarterback to get Justin Jefferson the ball. And the common denominator through all those quarterbacks, head coach Kevin O'Connell, needs to be questioned too.

The Vikings shouldn't completely fade away because the defense will keep them in every game. That was good enough for a 6-0 start. But the offense is simply too poor for the Vikings to remain in the top 10 of these power rankings.

Puka Nacua's knee injury is a massive blow for the Rams and their worst nightmare because receiver depth was the weakest part of the roster. Davante Adams is on injured reserve and Nacua is likely to join him, without a clear idea on when either player will be back. In a competitive NFC — there are three viable wild-card contenders in the NFC North, another in the NFC West outside of the Rams and only three spots for all of them — that dearth puts the Rams in danger of missing the playoffs.

Nacua was the fulcrum of the Rams' offense. On Sunday, he had 150 receiving yards and nobody else had more than 20. He got 19 of the Rams' 41 targets. Nobody other than Nacua and Adams has more than 287 receiving yards this season. The Nacua injury looks like the one the Rams couldn't afford to have happen.

The Steelers can take a huge step toward the AFC North title. They play the Bengals on Sunday night and will have a big rest edge. They're coming off a bye while the Bengals will play right after having a game in Spain, which is a tough turnaround. With a win the Steelers will clinch the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Bengals because of a season sweep.

In the first meeting, the Steelers won 30-27 and outgained the Bengals 411-352. They allowed Joe Burrow to throw for 282 yards and three touchdowns but also got 292 passing yards from Aaron Rodgers, 127 rushing yards from Jaylen Warren and took advantage of a muffed punt and a huge roughing the punter penalty by Cincinnati in the second half. Sunday's rematch will go a long way in determining the division champion.

Christian Gonzalez is a good cornerback who had a horrific game against the Packers. He allowed 105 yards to Matthew Golden and 82 to Christian Watson, according to Next Gen Stats. He's the first player to give up 80 yards to two different players in the same game since at least 2018, according to Next Gen Stats. He had allowed only 196 yards in coverage over his first six games combined, according to NGS .

Gonzalez should rebound but it was a shockingly bad game from him.

"When your best players don't play good, you don't have much of a chance in this league," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said, according to the team's transcripts. "So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more. We need more from him and everybody else. It wasn't just him."

The Texans' playoff odds are up to 43.9%, according to DVOA , and they'd be a team that nobody would want to face in the postseason. Their defense hasn't been great but the talent is there and it could emerge as a top-five unit in the second half. The real difference in the overall team is quarterback C.J. Stroud playing like he did as a rookie.

Stroud had five touchdowns Sunday, and even if that came against the Chargers, he has mostly had a good season. He's up to 10th among quarterbacks in adjusted EPA per play. The next three QBs on the list are Caleb Williams, Patrick Mahomes and Matthew Stafford.

"I beat myself up a lot when I don't do great, so I'm going to enjoy this and celebrate with my friends, family and teammates because I know what it feels like to throw a couple interceptions," Stroud said, via Texans Wire . "So, you need to be positive towards yourself."

When linebacker Arvell Reese, who was projected by some to go second overall in the NFL Draft, fell to the Giants at No. 5 everyone knew it was a great pick. Especially the Giants.

"He's gotten better every single year, playing off the ball and on the ball, so he does both," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the draft, according to the team's site . "Probably why he was our highest-rated non-quarterback player in the draft. He's an exciting player. We are fired up to have him."

Reese is now the favorite at about the midseason point to win NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year. On Sunday, he had 12 tackles and three sacks and was probably the best player on the field in the Giants' 19-11 win against the Eagles. For the season, he has 68 tackles and 4.5 sacks. He's going to be a star. The Cardinals took a running back instead of Reese in the draft. The Giants should thank them.

The Buccaneers' loss to the Bears might be the most impressive performance the NFC South has had in many weeks. That says something about the division, but Tampa Bay went into Chicago to face one of the NFL's hottest teams and, after a slow start, shut down its offense and was tied until the final seconds of the game, when the Bears kicked a game-winning field goal. Had head coach Todd Bowles been more aggressive on some of his decisions to kick short field goals , perhaps Tampa Bay would have won.

Bowles' game management might be an issue in the Buccaneers' quest for a division title but there are things coming together. The run game, led by Bucky Irving, leads the NFL in yardage and is second in yards per carry. The defense now ranks first in DVOA . Another factor in Tampa Bay's favor: It faces, by far, the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL, according to DVOA. The Bucs, who are three games under .500, look like the best pick to win that division and host a playoff game.

The Browns are going back to Deshaun Watson at quarterback, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, even after Shedeur Sanders had multiple clutch drives against the Saints and came a 2-point conversion in overtime of leading a big road win over the Saints. Sanders wasn't perfect, but Watson hasn't been either. Sanders had a 112.3 passer rating on Sunday. Watson's passer rating this season is 91.2 and he has taken a league-high 33 sacks.

Browns head coach Todd Monken wouldn't reveal his decision Monday, but apparently the Browns believe in quarterback wins so Watson will take his job back after missing last week (concussion protocol). If the Browns do go back to Watson it will lead to a quarterback controversy every time Watson struggles. Monken praised Sanders after Sunday's game.

"He wasn't perfect. I wasn't perfect," Monken said after the game, via USA Today . "But for a guy that really hasn't taken snaps with the ones in 10 weeks ... to come in there and continue to battle — really, really proud of him."

The Raiders were fairly good on defense early in the season, but that probably had to do with facing the Dolphins and Chargers. After giving up 414 yards and 38 points to the 49ers, the Raiders are 32nd in the NFL in yards and points allowed per game. They're allowing 6.1 yards per play, which is tied for the worst mark in the NFL.

There's not much hope of being a playoff contender with a defense that bad. This leads to questions over what the team should do, specifically as it pertains to making a quarterback switch to Fernando Mendoza. Kirk Cousins didn't make a great statement to keep his job with three second-half interceptions against the 49ers. That adds to the trade rumors following Cousins .

"It feels a little bit out of my hands, and I'll let the decision-makers make the decisions and react accordingly," Cousins said after the game about trade talk, according to Sporting News . "I love it here and love the guys here."

With 1:37 left in Sunday's game, the Cowboys fell behind a Colts team that had previously traded two of its best players and was embarrassed 42-7 by the Jaguars the week before. The Cowboys won, with a huge 46-yard completion to Ryan Flournoy leading to a game-winning touchdown, but it was still a performance that showed the Cowboys are not capable of being much better than they've been this season. Had they lost, there would have been serious questions about whether players like George Pickens should be traded from a 3-6 team. Instead, the Cowboys stayed alive in the NFC East.

If there was a positive that gives hope for a better second half, Dallas' defense played its best game of the season. It came against an Indianapolis offense that has been miserable, but Dallas will take progress where it can get it. The Cowboys allowed a season-low 271 yards. The Colts had 70 net yards and seven points (on a 19-yard drive after a turnover) through their first eight drives. Rookie safety Caleb Downs had a long-awaited impact with a sack and a game-sealing interception. The Cowboys' defense isn't suddenly good, but at least there can be optimism it's getting better.

The Panthers have lost three in a row and we're probably seeing who they truly are. Carolina passed for at least 262 yards in each of its first five games. Over the last three games it hasn't topped 257. Those MVP chants for Bryce Young seem like a long time ago. The Panthers' defense hasn't been great all season, but it has been worse lately, allowing at least 26 points in three straight games. Multiple injuries have played a part in the slump.

And yet, the Panthers are tied for first place in the division and should be in the race all season because nobody else in the NFC South seems capable of separating from the pack.

"We've got everything in front of us," defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton told the team's site . "So, it's just exciting. It really does seem like there's like a sense of hope, like there's not despair around here. Like you feel like you're on the right track."

The Saints started 1-4, got close wins over the Giants and Browns (they needed to stop a 2-point conversion in overtime to beat the Browns, using backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders, at home) and all of a sudden New Orleans is tied for first place.

The Saints still haven't shown much, but they could end up being the best team in the division. Receiver Jordyn Tyson, the eighth overall draft pick, made his debut Sunday after recovering from a hamstring injury. He had just 30 yards but he will make an impact as the season goes on. Also, running back Travis Etienne Jr. will return at some point from a hamstring injury. Those two players can transform an offense that desperately needs playmakers other than Chris Olave. In a bad division, that might be enough to get the Saints to the top.

Expecting Jacoby Brissett to save the season ignores that quarterback hasn't been the only problem in Baltimore. The Ravens' defense has stumbled badly when the team needed it to lead the way. Baltimore has lost four straight, giving up 35, 36 and 33 points the past three games. It is 26th in EPA allowed per play over those three games, including 28th in EPA per pass dropback allowed. Edge rusher Trey Hendrickson, Baltimore's major offseason addition after nixing the Maxx Crosby trade, has just two sacks as he continues to play through a finger injury.

There's an argument to be made that the defense has been bad because the offense can't sustain drives. Baltimore has 68 and 55 passing yards its last two games. Brissett will help that situation. But the Ravens need to start executing Jesse Minter's defense much better.

24. Washington Commanders (2-5-1, LW: 23)

Jayden Daniels set the stakes for Thursday night's game against the Giants, when asked after the team's loss to the Rams whether time is running out to get back in the NFC East race.

"Yeah. I think next week is a must-win," Daniels told reporters after the game.

He's right. With a win, the Commanders would be two games behind the Giants for first place and hold the tiebreaker, since the teams tied in their first meeting. That's not easy, but Washington wouldn't be dead. If the Commanders lose, they'd be four games back and not have the tiebreaker, which would probably be impossible to overcome. It might not matter because the Commanders aren't very good — they're 20th in DVOA with matching ranks of 20th on offense and defense — but at least with a win they'd have something to keep playing for.

The trade of safety Jessie Bates III was interesting. On one hand, the Falcons shouldn't turn down a second-round and fifth-round draft pick from Jacksonville for Bates, who is a very good player but also on the last year of his contract. That's exceptional value for a team that is three games under .500. It also goes against the general code of the NFL in that teams don't generally sell when they can still make the playoffs. The Falcons might be bad but so is the rest of the NFC South. They're just a half-game out of first place.

The trade made great sense from a big-picture perspective, but head coach Kevin Stefanski now faces a challenge: to get the team to still play like it's in the race to win a division championship even after trading away one of its best players.

Jacoby Brissett was benched and traded, and the Cardinals' job was going to go to Gardner Minshew for a few weeks before the team turned to rookie Carson Beck. That timetable might speed up. Minshew is feared to have a torn UCL in his throwing elbow and could miss the rest of the season, according to NFL Media .

That would press Beck into the lineup, and presumably a couple of games earlier than the team wants. The Cardinals' next two games are against the Rams and Chiefs, two talented and well-coached defenses. After that comes a three-game homestand against the Commanders, Eagles and Jets. Week 12 seemed like the right spot for Beck to get his first start, but Minshew's injury could change that. Beck, the first pick of the third round in this year's NFL Draft, had an intriguing performance in the Hall of Fame Game to start the preseason, but that isn't exactly stellar competition. The Cardinals will apparently get to see if he can follow that up in the regular season, whether they're ready for his debut or not.

The story of the Dolphins' loss to the Lions on Sunday was familiar to their season. There were plenty of mistakes, like 11 penalties that contributed to the offense not scoring a touchdown. QB Malik Willis was inconsistent. Miami faded in the second half. It did things a bad team generally does to lose games.

But the Dolphins' defense played very well, limiting a very good Lions offense to 19 points. And there is still fight from a team whose playoff hopes were nil before the season even started.

"I'm encouraged with this team," Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said, according to the Palm Beach Post . "I'm encouraged the way they work. I'm encouraged because we've challenged them to play the game a certain way. I'm encouraged because we've asked them to practice a certain way. I'm encouraged because, in my opinion, the Detroit Lions are probably the most physical team in the world. … And that's the way they coach and that's the way we play. And I would say we went toe to toe with them."

The question for the Titans will be what their team looks like after the trade deadline. They went into the bye after a win over the Colts, a three-point loss to the Browns and an overtime loss to the Bengals. That's progress for a Titans team that didn't have much to be excited about during an 0-5 start.

The focus of the second half of the season will remain quarterback Cam Ward and whether he can keep showing signs of progress. He had 304 yards and two touchdowns against the Bengals, and Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner proclaimed it Ward's "best game as a pro."

"If you want to see good quarterback play and the steps that it takes to be good, there's a lot of that stuff in this video, and I hope there's a bunch of people watching it," Warner said, via Titans Wire .

Switching to Joe Milton at quarterback didn't work out in a frustrating 19-11 loss to the Giants. Milton had 169 yards passing, never completing a pass of more than 20 yards, and took seven sacks. The Eagles scored one touchdown on 13 possessions. It's not a surprise that Milton didn't play well, especially with all the injuries around him, but it was another reminder that this Eagles season is going nowhere. It won't get better with defensive tackle Jordan Davis off to the Jaguars, who paid the hefty price of a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for him.

The offense in particular has been terrible and Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni didn't rule out changes to his staff. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion hasn't been any better than last season's coordinator, Kevin Patullo, and his job status is a topic of conversation in Philadelphia.

"We'll talk," Sirianni said of potential changes, via Roundtable Sports . "Obviously, right now my job is to be there for our guys and to go watch the tape and go look through everything. I'll do anything I can to help this team win football games. I'll look at myself internally first and then go from there."

The Jets lost 35-12 to the Chiefs, were outgained 391-229, outscored 21-0 in the second half and had 58 yards in the second half.

"We were playing with a lot of fight and spirit," Jets quarterback Geno Smith said, according to the team's site . "I thought the same thing in the second half, but I think it just got away from us."

There are no Jets fans, or anyone who watched the Chiefs game, who would agree with Smith. The fight has left the Jets, who are 1-7 since a season-opening win over the Titans. Aaron Glenn's status as head coach seems to be a week-to-week proposition, and everyone knows he's almost certainly not coming back in 2027. Don't expect many more wins this season.

Cornerback Sauce Gardner gave up the game-turning play, a 46-yard catch to Ryan Flournoy in the final two minutes that led to a go-ahead Cowboys touchdown. Receiver Josh Downs had 24 yards on three catches and said "I stunk today," via the team's site. Jonathan Taylor lost his fourth fumble of the season. Daniel Jones didn't have 50 yards passing against a suspect Cowboys defense until the final 1:30 of the first half. He finished with a 70.7 passer rating.

Everything is bad for the Colts right now. They had a chance to beat the Cowboys to at least save some pride, but made too many mistakes. It was disheartening how many of those mistakes came from their high-priced players. The trade deadline will likely see more players shipped off, and the Colts' season will get even more depressing.

"That's unacceptable," Gardner said of giving up the catch to Flournoy, according to the team's site . "I gotta be better. I gotta make the play, no matter what plays I made before that. At the end of the day, that's when my best is required."

Justin Herbert has six touchdowns and 11 interceptions this season. In every other NFL season he has thrown at least twice as many touchdowns as interceptions. He has never had a passer rating in a season below 93.4; this season it's 70.4. Herbert's precipitous drop, at age 28, is hard to believe. His offensive line isn't good. LA allowed eight sacks Sunday to Houston. Herbert's receivers have either been ineffective, or in Ladd McConkey's case, injured most of the season. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is clearly a bad fit for the talent on hand. Still, Herbert's play has been unfathomably bad.

And now he has an injury to his middle left finger that forced him out of Sunday's game. If he misses time, the Chargers could get even worse with DJ Uiagalelei replacing him. If Herbert plays, he simply is lost this season. In an honest moment last week on the "St. Brown Podcast," Rams safety Quentin Lake spoke about Herbert's inexplicable struggles.

"He was throwing deli meat out there," Lake said , comments he later apologized to Herbert for. "Bro, he's seeing ghosts. I don't know what's going on, but we knew we were going to get a couple [interceptions]. At least one."

articles.title: Mel Kiper Jr.'s New 2027 NFL Mock Draft Video Sees Jets, Dolphins Get QBs in Top 5 Picks
articles.summary: With Tuesday's NFL trade deadline looming, there are sure to be more draft picks switching teams as contenders look to bolster their roster with additions.
articles.body:
With Tuesday's NFL trade deadline looming, there are sure to be more draft picks switching teams as contenders look to bolster their roster with additions.

And that will have fans and front offices looking ahead to the 2027 NFL draft where a number of headline players, including some quarterbacks, will be available. With that in mind, ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. released a new mock draft that featured the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins landing signal-callers in the top-five picks.

Los Angeles Chargers: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

Tennessee Titans: Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas

Miami Dolphins: Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State

New York Jets (via IND): CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame

Philadelphia Eagles: Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

Smith is widely seen as the best player in college football, but whether he goes No. 1 or not will likely depend on if the team drafting with that top pick needs a quarterback.

If the Chargers assume Justin Herbert will return to form after his early season struggles, giving him a No. 1 option in Smith could lead to quite the connection in the immediate future.

As for the signal-callers, the overall picture has changed somewhat since early in the college football season. Dante Moore and Julian Sayin are out with long-term injuries, Arch Manning has dealt with inconsistency at times, and Darian Mensah is playing without go-to option Malachi Toney.

Carr has elevated himself in the meantime and has Notre Dame poised to make the College Football Playoff after Saturday's win over Miami. Then there is Mestemaker, who continues to put up massive numbers despite Oklahoma State losing multiple games in Big 12 play.

Kiper projected Mestemaker as the first quarterback taken at No. 3 overall, although he added there could be a "battle" between the two prospects to see who is the top signal-caller (14:55 mark).

"He has come so far in so short of a time," Kiper said when discussing Mestemaker (16-minute mark). "Can you imagine if he can make this quantum leap from where he was just a few years ago to where he is now in another couple years?"

In this situation, Carr won't have to wait long and goes No. 4 overall to the Jets.

That would give him a number of talented weapons, including Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr. and Mason Taylor, and it wouldn't be shocking if he found immediate success by just getting the ball into the playmakers' hands.

And it could lead to quite the Rookie of the Year battle with Mestemaker.

articles.title: Troy Aikman pokes fun at ESPN contract standoff during Bills-Vikings 'Monday Night Football' broadcast
articles.summary: Troy Aikman's diamond chain quip on Monday Night Football nodded at his stalled ESPN contract talks during the Bills' dominant 23-6 rout of Minnesota.
articles.body: Monday Night Football has recently felt like The Troy Aikman Show as the lead analyst wrestles with ESPN for a new contract, a stalemate that has reportedly created friction with booth partner Joe Buck. Aikman nodded to the standoff during the Week 9 matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings. Eyeing Justin Jefferson's heavily iced-out diamond chains, Aikman deadpanned, "I'm guessing that's insured. I cannot imagine wearing that on a football field. Can't imagine wearing it, period." CHARLES BARKLEY WEIGHS IN ON THE FRICTION IN THE 'MONDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL' BROADCAST BOOTH He then cracked that he might buy something similar, "if somebody would loan me some money ... " ESPN paused negotiations after Aikman's camp sought a market-resetting extension near $30 million per year. Tensions reportedly deepened because Aikman expected a deal before reaching his walk year, especially after Buck secured a six-year, $108 million extension. With contract talks tabled, sports television’s longest-running broadcast partnership faces an uncertain future beyond this season. ESPN ALLOWING TROY AIKMAN TO WALK AWAY FROM JOE BUCK BOOTH WOULD MAKE NO SENSE | BOBBY BURACK Prior to Monday, Aikman, 59, hadn't let his expiring deal or Bristol's boardroom standoff bleed into the broadcast. Whatever ESPN pays Aikman, it wasn't enough to sit through sixty minutes of Minnesota's offense. The Bills beat the Vikings, 23-6. The Vikes benched Carson Wentz with four minutes left, turning to backup Max Brosmer. Wentz managed just three passing yards in the first quarter, finishing with an 8.9 passer rating, 81 yards passing and three turnovers (two INTs, lost fumble). He fell to Buffalo's pass rush and turned Justin Jefferson into a ghost. Jefferson finished with three catches for 58 yards. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Aikman didn't sugarcoat Minnesota’s cratered offense. "I don't know how you fix it," he said. Lost in the collapse was a valiant effort by Minnesota's defense, which sacked Josh Allen four times. The win moves the Bills to 7-1 before heading to East Rutherford to face the New York Jets, while the 6-2 Vikings must sort out their quarterback mess before a Week 10 trip to Lambeau Field against the Green Bay Packers. articles.title: Justin Jefferson looked very frustrated as Vikings' offense struggled again in loss to Bills, leading to more trade speculation
articles.summary: The Vikings were booed repeatedly by their own fans in Monday night as their offense continued to struggle.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings struggled to get anything going offensively on Monday night, and Justin Jefferson seemed incredibly frustrated watching his team drop a second straight game.

The Vikings star wideout had just three catches for 58 yards in his team's 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills , and at one point was seen "seething" alone on the Vikings sideline. A broadcast shot showed Jefferson sitting on the bench in frustration.

It's easy to understand why Jefferson appeared upset. He hasn't had a 100-yard outing yet this season. Vikings fans at U.S. Bank Stadium weren't happy, either.

Carson Wentz started for the injured and also struggling Kyler Murray on Monday. He completed only eight passes and threw two bad interceptions on back-to-back drives. He should have thrown a third, but Terrel Bernard dropped it in the second half.

At one point, Wentz and the Vikings' offense was hit with a very loud chorus of boos from fans, something that happened repeatedly throughout the night.

The Vikings are still 6-2 on the season, but they've struggled at quarterback between Murray and Wentz. The Vikings' defense is among the best in the league, too, and did a good job slowing Josh Allen and a good Bills offense throughout the night. But without a capable offense — Wentz finished with an 8.9 passer rating — the defensive success doesn't matter much.

There has been plenty of speculation that the Vikings will make a move before the trade deadline Tuesday afternoon, including potentially landing a quarterback to take them the rest of the way. That, Jefferson said, isn't his job.

"I'm not sure … that's their job," Jefferson said. "My job is to continue to get open, continue to be the leader of the team and come next week, and hopefully things change."

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell declined to get into that speculation, too, when asked directly if they would make a move for a quarterback before the deadline.

"I'll defer to [general manager Nolan Teasley] on that," O'Connell said . "We've had dialogue about a lot of positions."

He did, though, rip his team's performance.

"In no way, shape or form was tonight acceptable," O'Connell said, via The Athletic's Alec Lewis . "I told the team that it starts with me. The defense was on the field too much … Just not even close offensively to what we want to be."

The Vikings don't have a lot of time to make a move before the deadline Tuesday afternoon, and there aren't a lot of good options for them available at quarterback.

It's clear the Vikings' offense needs a boost. They didn't get a first down until the fifth drive of the night Monday, and Wentz didn't complete a pass in the third quarter. Whether anything changes in order for them to take advantage of a 6-0 start, and Jefferson in the prime of his career, is still very much unknown.

articles.title: Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills dominate slumping Minnesota Vikings to improve to 7-1
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills improve to 7-1 on the season as they take advantage of a sputtering Minnesota Vikings in a 23-6 win on Monday night; the NFL returns to Europe on Sunday when the Detroit Lions face the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, live on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm
articles.body:
Linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams had interceptions and Tyler Bass made four field goals to stretch his franchise-record streak to 25 straight as the Bills (7-1) matched their best eight-game start since 1993. That season ended with their last of four straight Super Bowl losses.

With Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury, Carson Wentz started at quarterback for the Vikings (6-2) and didn't finish what became one of the worst performances of his 11-year career.

Wentz went 8 for 25 for 81 yards and three turnovers, including a backward pass in the first quarter that was thrown too high for even Justin Jefferson to catch it - resulting in a lost fumble near midfield.

Wentz, who was checked out in the medical tent at one point for an apparent lower leg injury, was replaced by Max Brosmer midway through the fourth quarter. Wentz completed 1 of 8 passes in the second half.

The battle of Buffalo's highest-scoring offense in the league against the least-scored-on defense might well have gone to Minnesota had the offense been able to muster a decent drive or two.

But the Vikings had four straight possessions in the first half start beyond their 40-yard line, and the furthest they made it was the Bills' 48.

The Vikings as usual sent blitzers at Allen from every angle possible, recording four sacks and an interception of a heave into the end zone that Byron Murphy ran down and returned 55 yards.

But the Bills eked out just enough in the first half to give themselves a cushion, when Allen found tight end Keleki Latu open in the back of the end zone for a 25-yard touchdown as he rolled right and was hit hard by Andrew Van Ginkel.

Rushing: James Cook, 31 carries, 107 yards, 1 TD

Receiving: Khalik Shakir, 4 catches, 58 yards

Passing: Carson Wentz, 8/25, 81 yards, 2 TDs

Rushing: Jordan Mason, 6 carries, 35 yards

Receiving: Justin Jefferson, 3 catches, 58 yards

articles.title: "Played the victim": Dianna Russini’s media return faces a new hurdle as analyst challenges her response to the Mike Vrabel controversy
articles.summary: Dianna Russini returns to sports media Wednesday, but analyst Jared Stillman is already pushing back.
articles.body: Dianna Russini returns to sports media Wednesday, but analyst Jared Stillman is already pushing back. Stillman called her recent People magazine interview about the Mike Vrabel scandal “so shameful” and said she is not the victim. Russini stepped down April 14 after photos of her with the Patriots head coach surfaced. Both denied any impropriety. Her new weekly show, “The Russini Report,” premieres November 11 on BetUS. Stillman’s criticism lands one day before that debut, and it centers on a single question: what exactly did she say was a lie?Analyst says Dianna Russini played the victim in her Mike Vrabel scandal interviewStillman took aim at Russini’s People interview on “Stillman and Company,” and his complaint comes down to one gap. She never says what the lies were.Russini told the magazine that the story spun out of her control.“The lies became so out of control. This was a runaway train, and there was nothing I could do to stop it. Once we realized nothing was going to stop this, it became unhealthy for us to read it because it wasn’t helping us heal. It was piling on and adding to what we were already dealing with,” she said.He argued she could have dodged the dishonesty talk by addressing what happened directly, and he used Vrabel as the contrast.“Dianna doesn’t even do that in her People magazine exclusive interview. Mike Vrabel addressed it; granted, in his own way. But when Vrabel gets up there, and he tells you that he’s hurt a lot of people that he’s really close with, he’s admitting that he did what he did,” the analyst said.Then he narrowed in on her wording. “Russini just says, ‘They lied.’ Lied about what, Dianna?”Russini also said it “quickly went from just one moment that people felt was true and erased years of work.” Stillman asked whether she meant only the Arizona photos. “One moment? The moment in Arizona? What about the moment in New York? What about all the other moments?” Older photos of the pair, taken March 11, 2020, at a New York City bar, resurfaced and were published in April.Two very different paths after the photosThe fallout split in two directions.Vrabel stayed with the Patriots. He admitted to difficult conversations with his family, staff and players, took responsibility for creating a distraction and started counseling. He declined to get into the specifics of his relationship with Russini.Russini stayed away from sports media. The Athletic found her undisclosed relationship with Vrabel broke its standards, though it did not rule on whether it was romantic. She is back with a one-hour live NFL show on the BetUS TV website and the platform’s X account, built around gambling analysis, game previews and matchup breakdowns.Stillman was unmoved by her talk of family support. “This isn’t something that everybody else did,” he said. “This is something you did.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Chiefs face a defining 2026 NFL trade deadline, and their next move could change the season
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are 6-2, yet the roster still has holes to fix before the NFL trade deadline hits at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs are 6-2, yet the roster still has holes to fix before the NFL trade deadline hits at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. Two recent losses to contenders have muddied the picture. Injuries have thinned the receiver group, and the tackle spots look shaky. General manager Brett Veach has almost no cap space but a healthy stash of draft picks. Head coach Andy Reid says he and Veach started trade talks about a month ago. What happens in the next few hours could decide how high this team can climb.The Chiefs’ 2026 trade deadline decision could shape the seasonA 6-2 record reads like a Super Bowl résumé. The film tells a messier story. Kansas City lost to two teams viewed as contenders, and the roster has gaps that wins can hide for only so long. A trade could settle the debate over what this team really is. Standing pat would send a message too, that the front office trusts what it already has.Deals must reach the league office by 4 p.m. ET, which is 3 p.m. at Arrowhead. Some moves could still be reported after the cutoff. Once it passes, released vested veterans go through waivers instead of straight to free agency.Kansas City has picks but almost no cap roomMoney is the obstacle. Estimates of Veach’s cap space run from $1.08 million at Over the Cap to $1.36 million from the NFLPA and $1.4 million at Spotrac. That rules out any big salary.Picks are a different matter. A first or second-rounder looks unlikely to move, but the Chiefs are projected to hold two third-round and two fourth-round picks in 2027, plus some late Day 3 selections to swap. The 2028 draft adds more. Veach can pay in picks if the player’s contract fits in the margin.Wide receiver is the biggest needReceiver is the loudest need, and it is not close. Rashee Rice has not found his peak form. Tyquan Thornton suffered a significant ankle injury, and Xavier Worthy went down with a hamstring problem.The free agent market looks bare, so a trade is the likeliest route unless the team brings back Tyreek Hill. A star is more of an offseason project. The middle ground has long been Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts. He would not save the season alone, but he could keep the offense from stalling.Tackle and edge rusher come nextTackle is messier. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson started better than anyone expected, but he is getting exposed more as weeks pass. Jaylon Moore appeared to suffer a lower-body injury Sunday, and Joshua Ezeudu replaced him at right tackle, a spot he did not mainly play with the Giants. Waiver pickup Diego Pounds sits unless Benson goes down. The cleanest fix costs nothing: Josh Simmons, the 2025 first-round pick, returning from injured reserve.Edge rusher is more of a luxury. The Chiefs sacked Geno Smith five times against the Jets, and Chris Jones had two. George Karlaftis and Ashton Gillotte held up. A quality backup tight end who blocks is a smaller wish.Reid and Mahomes trust Veach to decideReid says Veach handles the phone calls. “Brett does all of that,” Reid said. “If he gets to a point where something is up and he feels comfortable about it, then he hits me up on it.” Reid still carries weight on transactions, though he no longer runs the football operation as he once did in Philadelphia.Mahomes took the same line after the Jets win. “I leave that all up to Veach and coach Reid,” he said. He backed the players already in the building: “They’re ready to go out there and make plays when their number is called.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Week 10 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em for Smart Matchup Plays, Sleepers and More
articles.summary: We're officially past the midway point in the 2026 NFL season, which means, of course, that fantasy football playoffs are in the not-too-distant future. Week 10 will be an important one for managers on the fringes of contention, and it will open with a Thursday night NFC East showdown between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants.
articles.body:
We're officially past the midway point in the 2026 NFL season, which means, of course, that fantasy football playoffs are in the not-too-distant future. Week 10 will be an important one for managers on the fringes of contention, and it will open with a Thursday night NFC East showdown between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants.

Another 13 games will follow, as the Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be on bye.

In addition to bye week, managers will have to navigate numerous injuries. Here, you'll find early start/sit recommendations for the sort of second-tier stars many managers will need to consider in Week 10.

New England Patriots quarterback was drifting back into must-start territory before Sunday's disaster against the Green Bay Packers. The third-year signal-caller had another three-interception game, though he did do enough in garbage time to top 20 fantasy points.

Managers should trust Maye to come through again in Week 10, even if he gets a little reckless with the football again. The Patriots will need to put up points against the Detroit Lions, who haven't been particularly good defensively.

No team has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing QBs than Detroit.

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins has been a reliable streamer for most of the season. He has six games of at least 19.5 fantasy points in 2026 and is worth keeping as a matchup-based spot starter.

However, Cousins is coming off a disappointing 15.6-point outing against the San Francisco 49ers. He also faces another tough matchup against an NFC West contender in Week 10.

The Raiders will host the Seattle Seahawks, who have surrendered the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks.

Seahawks running back Jadarian Price has been back from injury for two games now, and while he didn't do much in Week 8, he flashed his receiving ability in Week 9.

Price caught four passes for 54 yards against the Arizona Cardinals and finished with 11.8 fantasy points on Sunday. He's a solid flex option this week against the Raiders.

Las Vegas has surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season.

The Cincinnati Bengals put on an offensive display against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. However, running back Chase Brown was only a bit player.

Brown did catch three passes and finish with 10.5 fantasy points. However, Samaje Perine actually led the Bengals in carries. This wasn't the first time in 2026 that Perine has led the ground attack. Given Cincinnati's shifting backfield situation, it's impossible to trust Brown against the rival Pittsburgh Steelers.

The Steelers have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs this season.

Amon-Ra St. Brown is the centerpiece of the Lions' passing attack and is a weekly must-start in all fantasy formats. However, he's likely to face standout cornerback Christian Gonzalez when Detroit hosts the Patriots in Week 10.

Gonzalez didn't have a great game against the Packers on Sunday, but he could still force Detroit to look in other directions. That bodes well for No. 2 receiver Jameson Williams, who will also be looking to bounce back in Week 10.

Williams had just two touches and five fantasy points on Sunday. However, he topped 16 fantasy points in point-per-reception (PPR) leagues in each of his previous four games.

While tight end Brock Bowers is a de facto No. 1 receiver, Tre Tucker is the Raiders' top perimeter option. While his production has been a bit up-and-down this season, Tucker has topped 20 points three times and had a solid 9.5 points in Week 9.

However, Tucker is likely to disappoint managers against Seattle. The Seahawks have surrendered an average of only 20.3 fantasy points to opposing receiving corps this season.

Bowers will remain a must-start against Seattle, but managers should eschew Tucker for WRs with better matchups.

Start: Eli Raridon, New England Patriots

Part of the issue for Drake Maye has been a lack of healthy options at wide receiver. A.J. Brown has been in and out of the lineup, while Romeo Doubs remains on injured reserve.

If the Patriots are going to keep pace with the Lions in Week 10, they'll probably need a big game from rookie tight end Eli Raridon.

Raridon caught three passes for 52 yards against the Packers, and he has a terrific matchup against Detroit this week. No team has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

Sit: Harold Fannin Jr., Cleveland Browns

With Shedeur Sanders in at quarterback, Cleveland Browns tight end Harold Fannin was largely ignored in the passing game until the very end of Sunday's game. He caught a 39-yard touchdown pass in overtime, but he was only targeted twice on the afternoon.

Fannin should see a bigger role in Week 10 if Deshaun Watson is back behind center. However, trusting him against the Houston Texans will be difficult.

Houston has surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing TEs this season.

articles.title: In 2023, Matthew Stafford bought Jennifer Lopez’s former Hidden Hills property for $28.2 million; his California estate got a major upgrade
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford and his wife Kelly closed on a newly built Hidden Hills mansion for about $28.2 million in December 2023.
articles.body: Matthew Stafford and his wife Kelly closed on a newly built Hidden Hills mansion for about $28.2 million in December 2023. The price set a record for the gated Los Angeles County community. The Rams quarterback bought the hilltop home on land that was once half of Jennifer Lopez’s estate, right next to a property the couple already owned. News of the deal spread in early 2024. Since then, the family has sold three older homes nearby and appears to have settled into the big one.How Matthew Stafford ended up with Jennifer Lopez’s old Hidden Hills landThe Staffords did not buy Lopez’s house. They bought the ground it once stood on.Lopez picked up the Hidden Hills estate in 2010 for $8.2 million and lived there until 2017, redecorating the main house along the way. Years after she left, the older mansion was bulldozed in 2021 and the lot was split into two parcels. A developer built a modern spec home on the hilltop half, and the Staffords bought it off market for $28.2 million. Some listings round it to $28.15 million, and the closing date was December 12, 2023.That figure beat the previous Hidden Hills record of $26 million, set earlier the same year. For a community known for horse trails, high walls and a long list of famous residents, it was a notable jump.What the new mansion offers compared with Jennifer Lopez’s eraThe old house is gone, so the comparison is really between two different ideas of a family home.The new property is a contemporary build on a high ridge. Reports put it at more than 15,000 square feet, while one deal database lists 17,129. Zillow describes it as a nine-bedroom, 12-bathroom home. The numbers vary by source, which is common with spec homes, where plans change during construction.One detail matters here. The house was still under construction when the Staffords bought it. That meant they were paying a record price for something not quite finished, a bet on the builder and the location as much as the finished product. It is a different kind of purchase from walking through a completed show home and writing a cheque.Why Stafford kept building a compound next doorThe mansion was never a standalone move. The Staffords already owned the neighboring property, a Hidden Hills home with a private vineyard that they bought in 2022 for $10.5 million. It has eight bedrooms, 10 bathrooms, a pool, gardens and a spa.Put the two together and the couple controlled roughly three acres. One deal tracker valued the combined holding at around $40 million.The logic is easy to follow. Stafford joined the Rams in 2021 after a trade from the Detroit Lions, and he won Super Bowl LVI with the team the following February. A quarterback with a young family and a demanding schedule values privacy and a short drive to work. Hidden Hills offers both, and reports have pointed to its distance from the team’s base as part of the appeal.There is also a quieter reason that gets less attention. Buying next door lets you control what is built next door. In a neighborhood where lots rarely come up, that has real value.What happened to the other Hidden Hills homesThe vineyard house was originally expected to serve as the family’s main residence. Then the bigger project came along and the plan appeared to shift.In 2022, the Staffords had also bought two ranch-style homes that once belonged to Drake, part of a group known as his “YOLO Estate.” They paid about $11 million for the pair. In September 2024, one went on the market at $6.8 million. A month later, the neighboring home was listed at $5.7 million. Both took price cuts and sat for a long time.In June 2026, the sales finally came through. The Real Deal, citing Realtor.com, reported that the Staffords sold all three homes for a combined $21.3 million in back-to-back deals within hours. The two ranches went to the same buyer behind one LLC. The larger vineyard home sold to a separate buyer for $9.7 million in an apparent off-market deal.Do the arithmetic and the Staffords bought for roughly $21.5 million and sold for $21.3 million. That is a small loss of about $200,000 on paper, before taxes, maintenance and years of holding costs. For people spending at this level, it reads less like an investment and more like clearing the decks.The timing also lines up with a good stretch on the field. Stafford signed a one-year extension worth $55 million and was named NFL MVP at the end of the 2025 season, according to The Real Deal. The sales sparked some online chatter about his future with the Rams, but nothing in the property records supports that. The family still owns the $28.2 million mansion, and every sign points to them living in it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Bills' Week 9 Game vs. Vikings
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills have taken a commanding lead in the AFC East and now sit all alone atop the conference with a 7-1 record.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have taken a commanding lead in the AFC East and now sit all alone atop the conference with a 7-1 record.

That's the reality after Buffalo took care of the Minnesota Vikings with a 23-6 road win on Monday Night Football.

Here are my grades for all of the key players from the victory.

The franchise centerpiece didn't put up gaudy numbers, but he found a groove as the game wore on and ultimately put together one of his strongest and most resilient efforts of the year.

With only two of the same starting offensive linemen from last week, Allen was under constant pressure in the first half. But he was still 21 of 31 for 234 yards with a touchdown and an interception (an ill-advised throw, albeit on a weird play call) while once again looking unstoppable on several key designed runs against an extremely strong defense.

Allen looked completely dialed in with his go-to targets for most of the night, especially as Buffalo pulled away in the second half.

As with Allen, it wasn't a fantasy football feast for Cook. But the three-time Pro Bowler deserves a lot of credit for sticking it out while getting blasted at or near the line of scrimmage for much of the first half.

Ultimately, Cook was one of the game's major difference-makers. His 31 carries were the second-highest mark of his career, as he somehow still managed to eclipse the century mark with 107 yards despite producing only 18 yards on his first 12 attempts.

Beyond that start, he averaged a strong 4.7 yards per rush, wearing the Minnesota defense down and allowing the Bills to dominate time of possession and control the game.

Johnson didn't get a lot of action as they kept relying on Cook, but he did catch both of the passes on which he was targeted and made a huge 36-yard grab down the sideline to convert a third-and-long on a second-half scoring drive.

It wasn't a standout game for the veteran No. 1, but he picked up 36 yards on four touches against a tough D, and there were no notable miscues.

Coleman left a play or two on the field, even if it was technically a drop-free performance. He gets points for a stellar contested first-down catch as the Bills were putting the game away in the fourth quarter.

It was a second consecutive tremendous showing for Shakir, who caught all four of the passes thrown his way for a team-high 58 yards. Allen is so comfortable with him on screens and timing routes. He might be more of a safety valve than any tight end on the roster.

Three catches on three targets for 28 yards in a fairly uneventful but unproblematic performance. A couple of those grabs were tricky. Have I mentioned this defense is good?

I mean, he was tied with Shakir for a team-high four catches. However, Knox was slow to pick up the rush on a sack that was very nearly an Allen fumble giving Minnesota the ball on the one-yard line, and he later dropped a would-be touchdown in the end zone.

The blocking was top-notch (one block particular helped Cook essentially ice the game), and he made a nice grab to move the chains on Buffalo's first touchdown drive.

You get a shoutout here when you're the fourth-string tight end and you sneak behind the defense for your first-ever NFL touchdown.

Grable did a superb job filling in for Spencer Brown at right tackle last week but faced an entirely different challenge in Dion Dawkins' stead against a terrifying defense this week. He often looked lost, surrendered pressure throughout the first half and was penalized twice.

Same story here, and it didn't help that Grable didn't have Alec Anderson while Corbett didn't have Dawkins. The veteran was beaten up all day in pass protection and as a run blocker.

There were a few key pressures in which McGovern was slow to help and deserved partial blame. But he was mauling defenders for Cook in the second half.

A near-pick from Dallas Turner had a lot to do with immediate pressure surrendered by Torrence, and that wasn't his only lapse in pass pro. However, he was easily the team's best run blocker.

He was a little rusty early in his return from injury, but very little pressure came from the right side and Brown also led the charge on some key Cook runs.

He had a couple of critical third-down pressures, but Chubb dropped a would-be pick-six and was held sackless for the sixth game in a row.

Rousseau once again got an arm on the opposing quarterback's hand as he released. He's clearly got a knack for it, which drastically increases the defense's turnover potential. Beyond that, he had a sack, a fumble recovery, a pass deflection, and another sack that was negated by a defensive holding penalty. What a year he's having.

He and Cole Bishop provided a strong initial push on Rousseau's sack of Carson Wentz, but besides that it was a low-impact performance for the oft-dominant sophomore.

The veteran wreaked havoc several times in the first half, particularly as a run-stuffer. He also provided the key push on a forced Wentz throw that should have been intercepted by Terrel Bernard.

I noted Sanders being in on a strong stop with Oliver on the very first defensive play of the game and then never noticed him again beyond a couple shoddy reps.

His tackling was basically perfect, and Bernard does seem to be playing better positional football altogether. He took a bad pass-interference penalty and was manhandled a couple of times in a short span as the Vikings established the ground game in the third quarter, but the 27-year-old made up for that with a key interception in a thoroughly strong performance.

He made a nice play and delivered good coverage on an interception that got Bernard off the hook for his DPI, and it was a strong overall effort from Williams. This linebacker duo is really finding a groove under Jim Leonhard.

It helped that Wentz forgot how to play quarterback, but Benford did a really good job throughout the night against one of the best receivers in the NFL.

The rookie still needs to clean up his game between now and the playoffs, but he had back-to-back wins against Justin Jefferson on a key third- and fourth-down sequence. Not bad for a 22-year-old second-round pick, even if he got away with a little more contact than is usually kosher on the fourth-down stop.

There was no major damage, and he made a great play stuffing Aaron Jones at the line of scrimmage to force a third down early in the second half.

It wasn't another monster game for Bishop, but he led the charge on Rousseau's sack and made a massive tackle to keep Jones short of the sticks and force Minnesota to settle for a field goal late in the first half.

His holding penalty cost Rousseau a sack. Nothing egregious beyond that, but Hamlin doesn't look like a guy you want playing a major role down the stretch. The awareness and instincts aren't there.

He was a perfect 3-for-3 (including one from 52 yards out), extending his streak to 24 consecutive made field goals. Combine that with no missed extra points and it was a perfect evening for the veteran.

It was actually the rookie's worst performance thus far, as he put nothing inside the 20 while settling for two touchbacks on five punts. That said, did you see that hit ?

Dortch brought the opening kickoff back 58 yards. He hardly had a chance to factor in beyond that.

The signal caller looked more like a quarterback playing in his first organized football game than a guy making his 101st NFL start. Wentz was handed the keys to the Vikings' offense after the team announced that Kyler Murray was dealing with a hamstring injury that head coach Kevin O’Connell described as a "week-to-week kind of thing." While the Vikings posted a 5-1 record with Murray under center early in the season, he's thrown five touchdowns and three interceptions, and the Vikings have leaned heavily on their defense to get the job done.
