articles.title: NFL power rankings: Bears, Packers and Lions go north; Patriots, Ravens regress for Week 10
articles.summary: How do all 32 teams in the NFL stack up after Week 9?
articles.body:
Week 9 in the NFL was full of some lopsided results. Eight games saw the winning team ahead by at least two possessions. Only three games going into Monday night were decided by four points or less.

There's some separation happening as the second half of the 2026 regular season is here. The best teams are playing better, while the worst teams seem to have attrition pile up against them.

Five teams — the Steelers , Bengals , Broncos , Bears and Lions — all have winning streaks of four or more games. Five other teams — the Jets , Ravens , Colts , Chargers and Eagles all have losing streaks of four or more games.

Putting all that into a blender, here's looking at how all 32 teams stack up against each other going into Week 10:

Brett Davis/Imagn Images via Reuters Connect

1. Buffalo Bills 7-1 (previous ranking: 1)

The Bills went into Monday night's game against the Vikings averaging a league-best 33.3 points per game, about a field goal ahead of the Bengals. They faced a Minnesota defense giving up a league-low 13.3 points per game. Offense won out in the compromise, right smack in the middle with 23 points, and most importantly, plenty enough to win.

Christian McCaffrey is surging toward the Hall of Fame after getting up to 18 career games with a rushing and receiving TD. The running game is less efficient than usual, but he has stayed healthy and effective thanks to emerging rookie steal Kaelon Black. The 49ers are up to eight receivers with scoring receptions from Brock Purdy this season.

The Bears somehow survived five turnovers against the Buccaneers because of their defense staying dominant in one area. They went into Sunday night allowing opponents to convert at only 23.8 percent on third down, and they held the Buccaneers to 2-for-12 (16.7 percent)

Bo Nix doesn't blow away anyone with big numbers, but he had a classic game in Carolina, spreading his 25 completions over eight players. Rushing for only 82 yards on the Panthers is worrisome, but they have found their versatile lead back in rookie Jonah Coleman.

Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are up to connecting for 9,360 passing/receiving yards, a new record for a quarterback and tight end combination. Kenneth Walker III is on pace for 24 total TDs and can challenge the single-season franchise record of 27.

The Jaguars are up to plus-9 in turnover differential to lead the NFL. No wonder their average margin of victory is 13.8 points per game. Jacksonville is running away with the AFC South, so it's just now a matter of whether it can lock down the No. 1 seed.

The Vikings went into Monday night's loss to the Bills averaging only 20 points per game, scoring at a pace with some of the league's worst teams. Carson Wentz failed to give them a spark with struggling Kyler Murray out. They can't win the high-scoring NFC North if they can't find more offense soon.

The Steelers are more confident they can win big in Aaron Rodgers' presumed final season. He's on pace to hit 27 touchdown passes for the 12th time in his career, but he would like to increase his career-low 6.5 yards per passing attempt.

The Seahawks got back to their ideal 50-50 offense to dominate the Cardinals, with 28 Drew Lock passes to match the number of non-Lock runs. The result was 120 rushing yards, finding the right groove with Zach Charbonnet and rookie Jadarian Price, with the latter becoming a receiving factor.

The Lions' once-maligned defense has allowed only a total of 62 points during their four-game winning streak. They will get a good test against the Patriots in Munich, Germany, in Week 10, where Jared Goff needs to shake off back-to-back sub 200-yard, one-INT games.

Joe Burrow, after picking apart the Falcons downfield in Spain, is up to a league-leading 74.0 completion percentage while still averaging a robust 8.0 yards per attempt. He's on pace for 5,070 passing yards and 49 TDs, which would be one of the all-time great passing seasons.

Matt Pendleton/Imagn Images via Reuters Connect

The Packers have proved once again Matt LaFleur is locked into their offensive strengths in a given season. They got up to 32 runs to match Jordan Love's 32 dropbacks in New England, but only because Love passed them to big plays and a big lead. This team is playing great complementary football, because jumping ahead also lets them tee off with pressure to force turnovers. Just wait if Micah Parsons can return.

The Rams have become very reliant on Puka Nacua to move the ball and Myles Garrett to clean up for their defense. But Nacua cannot shake injury issues and Garrett is just returning from his long absence. Nacua accounted for more than half of their offensive yards (170 of 334) against the Commanders to save the day. If he's out again, L.A. would have some real issues.

The Patriots, in their five wins, have seen Drake Maye throw a combined two interceptions. In their four losses, he has thrown a combined 9 interceptions. He's starting to press and force the issue in the passing game as the defense keeps struggling, not a good formula.

The Giants keep getting breaks in the schedule, where even some combination of J.J. McCarthy and Jameis Winston can give them a QB edge. They are winning several battles of attrition, just outlasting opponents, but they should not apologize for how much mental toughness John Harbaugh has instilled in them. So much for knocking him for the Ravens' blown leads.

The Browns' aggressive nature with first-year coach Todd Monken should be applauded. Even though they didn't win the overtime game in New Orleans, seeing their passing game click so much with Shedeur Sanders is inspiring. Making the playoffs is less important than finding out whether Sanders can be their franchise QB.

The Cowboys are a roller coaster with Brian Schottenheimer and their lack of reliable defense never makes a lead safe, especially when they get too enamored with Dak Prescott's passing. They outlasted the Colts with near-perfect balance, with 37 Prescott dropbacks matched by 34 total runs. That's the formula the Cowboys need: A lot more Javonte Williams.

C.J. Stroud lit up the Chargers for 384 yards and 5 TDs, bringing him up to an average of 281 yards per game and on pace for 34 TDs. He's averaging 8.0 yards per attempt with a 112.1 passer rating. He's all but locked up his lucrative second contract.

The Raiders went to San Francisco, allowing an average of 146.4 rushing yards per game, the second-highest total in the NFL. They gave up 190 to a 49ers combination led by McCaffrey and rookie Kaelon Black. They also only ran for 24. That kind of disparity doesn't add up to winning games.

The Ravens might be trying to move Derrick Henry, but they can't expect to be competitive without a mobile quarterback and with a shaky offensive line. They also need some semblance of a running game to keep from overexposing Jesse Minter's struggling defense. If Henry is traded, it would be waving the white flag in trying to be respectable the rest of the way.

The Buccaneers dropped to 1-6 in games outside the NFC South after losing a tough one in Chicago on Sunday night. They remain the NFL's top rushing offense, averaging 163.9 yards per game. They will hope to rev up the passing game after a needed Week 10 bye.

The Falcons, in losing to the Bengals in Madrid, saw Bijan Robinson post his first (exact) 100-yard rushing game since Week 4. When he hits the century mark, they are 2-1 and 1-5 otherwise. Michael Penix Jr. needs to be more consistent again after his hot start.

The Saints finally marched away with a home victory, working hard in overtime with a gritty Tyler Shough leading the offense to cool off the hot seat (a little) for Kellen Moore. Brandon Staley, however, may not be safe, as the defense is giving up an average of 27 points per game.

The Cardinals traded Brissett, which was the right move. They got a win from Gardner Minshew in Dallas, which was the right move. But after Minshew was ripped in Seattle, the next right move is starting rookie Carson Beck.

The Panthers' big defensive issue, with or without now-fired former defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero, has been staying on the field too much after third down. Opponents have converted around 54 percent against them. The Broncos were 6-for-10, even when held to 82 rushing yards by a horrible run defense.

The Commanders seem to have lost some trust in Jayden Daniels as a downfield passer without Terry McLaurin in David Blough's offense. The aggressive decision-making from Dan Quinn in Daniels' rookie season has been replaced with tentative, not-to-lose coaching, and it keeps costing the team. Sadly, it will also likely cost Quinn his job soon.

The Eagles have gone through Tanner McKee and Joe Milton III behind Jalen Hurts and have lost seven consecutive games. They are playing for next year in this unbelievable injury mess of a season. That means it's time to see what they have in rookie Cole Payton. Nick Sirianni should still be safe to keep his job, but he needs to play Payton with nothing left to lose.

Geno Smith had operated with a touchdown pass in seven consecutive games until the Garrett Wilson-less clunker in Kansas City, in which he rated a season-low 70.4. With the Jets free-falling out any wild-card contention, it might be time soon to evaluate rookie Cade Klubnik.

Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor each had a fourth-quarter turnover in a close loss to the Cowboys, which sums up the season for Shane Steichen's offense. Have both the QB and running back played their last down in Indianapolis? Backups Seth McGowan and Anthony Richardson may soon shake things up further.

The Titans hope the bye will lead to better play from Cam Ward in the second half of the season. He had his first two-TD pass game of the season and also ended a five-game interception streak in the Week 8 overtime thriller vs. the Bengals. The rub is facing the first-place Jaguars in two of the next three games.

The Dolphins, as expected, with their limited and inexperienced receiving corps, is No. 32 in the NFL with an average of only 164.8 passing yards per game. Malik Willis is doing all he can, but this is leading to having their pick of a franchise QB in the 2027 draft.

Justin Herbert increased his league-high interception total to 11 against the Texans. DJ Uiagalelei proved in mopup duty, however, why the Chargers are stuck, unable to make a real QB change. Losing key offensive line and receiving help are factors, but the ugliness has gotten to be too consistent.

articles.title: 4 quarterbacks Vikings must target before trade deadline to keep Super Bowl dreams alive
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings are suddenly confronting one of the NFL’s most uncomfortable questions: Can they still contend without dependable quarterback play? Aft...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are suddenly confronting one of the NFL's most uncomfortable questions: Can they still contend without dependable quarterback play? After opening the season with six straight victories, Minnesota has suffered consecutive defeats. Kyler Murray's hamstring injury has complicated matters . Carson Wentz's latest performance has intensified concerns about the team's depth under center . With the November 10 trade deadline approaching, general manager Nolan Teasley cannot afford to sit back and hope everything fixes itself. If Minnesota wants to keep its Super Bowl dreams alive, some four quarterbacks deserve serious consideration.

Minnesota's journey through the 2026 campaign has been a thrilling rollercoaster that has suddenly veered toward dangerous territory. The Vikings surged to a 6-0 start. They stood tall as the league's last undefeated team behind Brian Flores' dominant defense. Meanwhile, Aaron Jones Sr. supplied a physical ground attack. Will Reichard delivered reliable scoring, and Justin Jefferson remained an unstoppable perimeter threat. However, consecutive defeats against divisional rival Detroit and Buffalo have exposed an alarming offensive fragility.

In Week 9, Wentz completed just eight of 25 passes for 81 yards and threw two interceptions in a 23-6 loss to the Bills. Murray is considered week-to-week. That leaves Minnesota with no guarantee of an immediate solution. With Christian Darrisaw also dealing with concussion concerns and Donovan Jackson unavailable, the Vikings need to stabilize the offense before their promising season slips away.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

If Minnesota wants the most seamless potential reunion, Kirk Cousins should be at the top of its list. The veteran quarterback spent two seasons with Kevin O'Connell in Minnesota. That gives him familiarity with the coach's offensive philosophy. He also has established connections with Jefferson and TJ Hockenson.

Cousins is also producing in Las Vegas. Through nine games, he has thrown for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. That shows that he can still operate a productive passing offense. The complication is that the Raiders are 4-5 and remain within reach of the AFC playoff picture. They have little reason to surrender their starting quarterback cheaply. Minnesota would likely need to offer meaningful draft compensation to make the conversation worthwhile. Still, if the Raiders decide to prioritize their longer-term quarterback plans, Cousins could become an intriguing opportunity.

Mac Jones might represent the most practical alternative. Currently backing up Brock Purdy in San Francisco, Jones has experience operating within Kyle Shanahan's offensive system. That shares many principles with O'Connell's approach.

Jones also demonstrated his ability to handle a starting workload during his time in both New England and Jacksonville. He showed that he can distribute the football effectively when surrounded by capable playmakers. With Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Hockenson available, Minnesota could give him a considerably strong supporting cast. The 49ers, however, would need to be comfortable surrendering their insurance policy behind Purdy. A Day 3 selection could be an attractive starting point. Still, San Francisco's own injury concerns could make it reluctant to deal.

Daniel Jones offers a different profile., He combines mobility with considerable starting experience. He also has some familiarity with Minnesota after spending time on the Vikings' practice squad in 2024. That background could help him navigate the transition.

His 2026 production in Indianapolis has been uneven, with 1,722 passing yards, six touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Those numbers raise legitimate questions about whether he would provide the stability Minnesota needs. Nevertheless, his ability to extend plays could help compensate for an offensive line dealing with injuries. If the Colts are willing to discuss a short-term arrangement, Jones deserves consideration.

Geno Smith would be the boldest option on this list. The veteran quarterback still possesses the arm talent and downfield accuracy to energize Minnesota's passing game. Smith has thrown for 2,078 yards, 12 touchdowns and just three interceptions through nine games. That makes him an attractive potential acquisition.

The challenge is persuading the Jets to move their starting quarterback. Smith is also a team captain. His production gives New York little incentive to surrender him without a substantial return. Minnesota would need to make an aggressive offer. Still, if the Jets decide to reshape their direction, Smith could immediately restore some vertical life to the Vikings' offense.

The Vikings have too much talent to let their season unravel. Cousins offers familiarity, and Mac Jones provides a potentially affordable system fit. Daniel Jones brings mobility, and Smith delivers proven downfield production. None is a perfect solution. That said, after the Bills loss, standing pat would be an equally dangerous gamble. Teasley must explore every realistic avenue at the deadline . The Vikings' championship window is still open, but it needs a quarterback capable of keeping it that way.

articles.title: Bears’ Tyson Bagent Trade Window Reopens Hours Before NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears may have a last-ditch opportunity to trade backup quarterback Tyson Bagent in the final hours before the 2026 NFL deadline. The post Bears’...
articles.body:
If the Chicago Bears are open to moving quarterback Tyson Bagent after last week's trade buzz, they may have just found a new suitor hours before the NFL deadline.

Bagent became the subject of trade speculation last week when Sports Illustrated's Jason La Canfora reported that the Baltimore Ravens "initiated trade talks" with the Bears about the possibility of acquiring their No. 2 quarterback in the wake of losing starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley to significant injuries.

The Ravens do have a link to Bagent with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, who worked with him in the same role in Chicago during Ben Johnson's first season in 2025.

Ultimately, the Ravens opted to acquire veteran Jacoby Brissett as their fill-in starter from the Arizona Cardinals, who had benched him for veteran Gardner Minshew.

In an interesting turn of events, though, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday that Minshew will likely need season-ending surgery after tearing his UCL during Week 9's start, potentially creating a new Bagent suitor who had previously reported interest.

Offseason Trade Rumors Linked Tyson Bagent to Cardinals

Bagent might seem like a long-shot option for the Cardinals in their current predicament, but the trade speculation has at least some prior basis.

Back in February, when the Cardinals were still figuring out their 2026 quarterback plans, longtime Arizona sports radio host John Gambadoro reported that the team was "intrigued" with Bagent as a potential trade target.

Weeks later, Bears general manager Ryan Poles confirmed that they had received trade interest in Bagent earlier in the offseason — though he did not specify which teams.

The link is still a little flimsy. But if the Cardinals had interest in Bagent before and are looking on the trade market for a Minshew replacement to carry them through the second half of the 2026 season, perhaps they will call the Bears before the deadline.

Bears Trade Deadline: Could Another QB Draw Interest?

The Bears will likely be busy working the phones in the remaining hours before the NFL trade deadline arrives at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10.

Insiders have frequently suggested that the Bears are still looking for defensive upgrades on the trade market in the 12 days since they traded two first-round picks for superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who has already made an impact.

Could Chicago get calls about Case Keenum's availability, too?

Keenum — the Bears' third-string quarterback — impressed against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 3, throwing for 247 yards and two touchdowns in his first start in more than 1,000 days and guiding the Bears to a 27-7 rout.

"[The Bears are] another team that I don't think would be moving players. But teams always need QB help, and Keenum showed a little something earlier this season in relief of Caleb Williams ," ESPN's Dan Graziano floated on November 4. "For the right offer, who knows?"

Bears head coach Ben Johnson might not want to meddle with the synergy of his quarterback room, but a strong trade offer for either Bagent or Keenum could persuade Poles and Chicago's front office to act before the deadline passes today.

We have reached the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season.

And the order for the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft is taking shape.

The New York Jets sit in the fourth spot for now, holding the rights to the Indianapolis Colts' first pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, thanks to the Sauce Gardner trade. The Jets are one of four teams with multiple picks in the first round next spring. Cleveland holds their own pick (at No. 16) and the Los Angeles Rams' pick (No. 18) due to the Myles Garrett trade.

The Titans have the No. 30 pick from the Chicago Bears, as part of the Jeffery Simmons deal.

articles.title: Dolphins vs. Colts odds: Opening lines for Week 10 matchup
articles.summary: Tuesday’s trade deadline could shake up the Week 10 odds, especially in the Dolphins at Colts game.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins face off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, a game featuring two teams vying for the first-overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Well, technically. The Colts, 2-7, could claim the top spot, but they do not own their own first-round for the next draft, with the New York Jets holding that selection as part of an in-season trade last year that sent cornerback Sauce Gardner to Indianapolis.

Despite the Dolphins' positive signs of growth over the past several weeks, the oddsmakers have given the Colts a slight nod in this game. The FanDuel Sportsbook line opened with Indianapolis favored by 2.5 points , slightly under the typical three-point advantage given to a home team, and it has remained steady as of Tuesday morning.

The point total is set at 40.5, while Miami is +116 on the money line for the straight-up win. The Colts are -136 for the win.

This week could see massive changes in odds as Tuesday's trade deadline approaches. Indianapolis is expected to be sellers today, with running back Jonathan Taylor considered one of the top available players on the market, and rumors swirling around defensive tackle Grover Stewart and quarterback Daniel Jones. If the Colts do start making trades ahead of the 4 p.m. Eastern deadline, how will the line move?

Miami could also be sellers, with teams reportedly interested in players like linebacker Jordyn Brooks and defensive tackle Zach Sieler. The Dolphins may not be eager to move on from core pieces of their rebuild, but they may be offered a package of draft picks they cannot refuse.

Tuesday could significantly affect the odds for this weekend's game, but for now, the Colts are slightly favored.

articles.title: NFL analyst calls out Falcons' 'most-critical' error against Bengals
articles.summary: Jawaan Taylor flags killed Atlanta against Cincinnati
articles.body:
Despite being outgunned by the Cincinnati Bengals and their loaded offense, the Atlanta Falcons had their chances to make Sunday's game in Spain a competitive one. Unfortunately, the Falcons shot themselves in the foot on a couple of key possessions when they had a chance to narrow the gap.

Those mistakes proved costly as the team lost by a final score of 34-17. Over at NFL.com , they have detailed those mistakes in their recap for Week 9.

"The Falcons O-line committed two fouls in the red zone on their second drive, leading to the first field goal of a touchdown fight. Its most critical error, though, came at the start of the fourth quarter, when down two TDs at the Bengals' 10-yard line, Atlanta was called for offensive holding on a third-and-2 incompletion. Cincy accepted the penalty and forced a fourth-and-12. Settling for cutting a two-score lead to a ... two-score lead, Nick Folk instead shanked a 38-yard field goal, and the Bengals' lead held at 14."

While they didn't name him, the guy responsible for the hold in the fourth quarter was right tackle Jawaan Taylor, who came to Atlanta leading the league in penalties over the last few years and has been unable to shed the bad habit.

The Falcons were put into a bind by the retirement of Kaleb McGary, and for a sudden replacement Taylor wasn't a terrible option. However, what he's put on tape has been pretty disappointing this season. In addition to the ongoing penalty problem, Taylor is grading out at 55.3 for the season , which ranks 65th out of 71 qualifying tackles.

Needless to say, the Falcons front office will need to replace Taylor this coming offseason - and they'll have plenty of assets to do so with four top-100 picks and nearly $150 million in cap space.

articles.title: NFL insider shares Jonathan Taylor’s ‘three possible outcomes’ ahead of trade deadline
articles.summary: The trade deadline is nearing and Jonathan Taylor’s future with the Indianapolis Colts still remains up in the air. It had been reported in recent weeks that...
articles.body:
The trade deadline is nearing and Jonathan Taylor's future with the Indianapolis Colts still remains up in the air.

It had been reported in recent weeks that Carlie Irsay-Gordon had opened up to the possibility of allowing Taylor to leave the team. However, it would seem as if the Colts are yet to receive an offer that they would be inclined to accept.

Taylor is one of the few stars left in Indianapolis following the exits of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner at the end of last month. There is still the possibility that he could depart over the coming hours, though.

Jonathan Taylor's three possible trade deadline outcomes

After their latest loss at the weekend, Taylor admitted he was preparing for all possibilities over the coming hours, as he shared his gratitude to the fans in Indianapolis. As the running back accepted the possibility of leaving, as things stand, he could be playing for the Colts on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins.

"Things can change. Talking to teams that have checked in on Taylor, they've felt like the price has been too high. It may be that Indy sticks to that because he is relatively young and he's under contract for two more years. They don't have to trade him. That's the position they've been taking," said Dan Graziano.

"There are three possible outcomes here in the final 48 hours. One, Indianapolis can lower its price, do a deal and just move on, kickstarting the full-on rebuild. Two, a team could come up to Indianapolis' price, overpay for Jonathan Taylor, and then the Colts feel better about sending him away.

"Or three, he could still be a Colt at 4:01 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, which I have always believed, and continue to believe, is an extremely possible outcome. So, yeah, I wish I could tell you more, but here's what I know. Teams that have checked in have been turned off by the price.

"Oftentimes on Monday, the day before the trade deadline, when teams check in again, sometimes they're told different things. It's possible that will happen again on Monday. But if Jonathan Taylor is still a Colt at the end of this week, I don't believe anyone should be stunned."

Having racked up eight touchdowns and 656 rushing yards on the season, it is no surprise that teams are showing an interest in Taylor. However, the Colts will naturally be looking to add a first-round draft pick for next year.

There are currently seven other backs who have tallied more rushing yards than Taylor this season, and the league-leader, Bijan Robinson, is currently over 200 yards ahead of Taylor. Unless a team becomes desperate in the final hours, it feels unlikely that a huge offer for Taylor will be sent.

articles.title: Las Vegas Raiders insiders have identified exactly why they’re struggling this season
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders went 3-0 to start the 2026/27 NFL season but their form has quickly declined. After nine weeks of the current campaign, they are now si...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders went 3-0 to start the 2026/27 NFL season but their form has quickly declined.

After nine weeks of the current campaign, they are now sitting with a 4-5 record and are third in the AFC West.

Amid their struggles, Dan Graziano has been speaking to NFL on ESPN about what people within the Raiders have been saying about their struggles.

In their eyes, Graziano revealed that people think they don't have 'enough beef up front', while their defence is also a problem, with suggestions that 'their defensive line is ultra-vulnerable'.

He explained: "When I talk to Raiders people, the way they feel about it is that they just don't have enough beef up front.

"The interior of their defensive line is ultra-vulnerable. They have young guys on the back end.

"It just doesn't feel like there's enough there on the depth chart for the Raiders to be a very good defence at this point. And that's why they're going to have games like this."

The Raiders' last game saw them lose 38-17 against the high-flying San Francisco 49ers.

They are due to take to the field again on Sunday, November 15, against a Seattle Seahawks team who have also struggled somewhat this term. The Seahawks are 5-4 after losing just three games in the previous campaign.

articles.title: Packers soar into top 10 of NFL power rankings after dominant win in NE
articles.summary: The Packers have soared into the top 10 of the NFL power rankings for the first time in the 2026 season following Sunday's dominant win over the Patriots.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers jumped into the top 10 of USA Today's NFL power rankings for the first time during the 2026 season after beating the New England Patriots convincingly on Sunday at Gillette Stadium.

The 45-27 win over the defending AFC champs and the elite play of quarterback Jordan Love prompted Nate Davis to move the Packers up four spots to No. 7 entering Week 10.

From Davis: "Just when it seems like it's all coming together − OLB Micah Parsons nearing his return, the running game nearing its return − RB Josh Jacobs is going back on the shelf for a group that's won six of seven. But if mad bomber Jordan Love keeps launching precision munitions, the rest may not matter."

Davis wasn't alone. Five of the other six power rankings reviewed had the Packers moving up into the top 10. It seems Matt LaFleur's team has finally won over detractors with five victories in the last six weeks.

But even sitting at 6-3, the Packers are in last place in the NFC North and holding the No. 7 seed in the NFC playoff race, so there's plenty of work to be done with eight games to go. Starting Sunday in Green Bay.

The Packers host the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10. Kevin O'Connell's team dropped out of the top 10, falling to No. 11, after a deflating home loss in primetime to the Buffalo Bills to end Week 9. The Vikings have a major quarterback issue and will be coming to Lambeau Field with a rest disadvantage on Sunday. Can the Packers keep piling up big wins? Any chance of winning the NFC North in 2026 probably rests on beating the visiting Vikings this week.

Packers-Vikings in November football at Lambeau Field. "Let the show begin," as Micah Parsons said last week.

Packers power rankings by week (USA Today)

Here's where the Packers rank in other national power rankings entering Week 10:

From Rob Demovsky on most important game left : "How can it not be one of the remaining NFC North games, you ask? Yes, next Sunday against the Vikings is huge. So is Week 16 at the Bears. So is Week 18 against the Lions. But given the likelihood that one of those other teams will win the NFC North, the Packers might need to make sure the Rams don't catch them for an NFC wild-card spot. As damaging as a loss to a division team would be, so would a loss to another NFC team they might need the head-to-head tiebreaker against."

From Conor Orr : "Here's why I love what I do (honestly): I spent all offseason studying the run game, heavier personnel packages and the increased usage of 21 personnel. Jordan Love is going to come out and throw for 5,000 yards (seriously) with no running game to speak of whatsoever and the Packers are one of the best teams in the NFL."

From Frank Schwab : "Whatever was happening the first three weeks of the season with the Packers, they're far beyond that. Green Bay is 5-1 since a slow start. Since Week 4 it is fifth in EPA per play on offense and third in EPA per play allowed on defense. The Packers take a jump in the rankings for two reasons: The offense looked great again against the Patriots on Sunday, and Micah Parsons' return is looming for the defense. It is very easy to forget that when Parsons tore his ACL last season the Packers were 9-3-1 and leading in the second half at Denver. And Green Bay has been playing much better on defense the past six games. Josh Jacobs' broken finger could have a negative effect. He will have finger surgery and miss a maximum of three weeks, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. The Packers' running game has been horrible all season but a little better with Jacobs. Taking a step back in the run game could also affect the passing game, which has been cooking with Jordan Love turning Matthew Golden and Christian Watson into one of the NFL's top receiving duos."

From Pete Prisco : "Jordan Love and the passing game get a lot of the attention, but that defense has really impressed. When they get Micah Parsons back, look out."

From Josh Kendall and Chad Graff on midseason grade : "A-. The Packers' pass defense has quietly been among the best in the league, and they soon get to welcome back arguably the sport's best pass rusher in Micah Parsons. It's still fair to wonder if their lack of a running game will haunt them, but Jordan Love is playing like an MVP, and Matthew Golden and Christian Watson are a heck of a receiving duo.

From Ralph Vacchiano : "It's a big jump, but the Packers earned it by pounding the Patriots in New England. More than that, they are playing outstanding on defense, and they are showing off a passing game that might just be the best in the league (or at least outside of Cincinnati). It's hard to find a quarterback playing better than Jordan Love, and it's impossible to find a receiving tandem better than Christian Watson and Matthew Golden at the moment. If this team had a running game — I mean, any semblance of a running game at all — they might be the best team in the NFC. As it is, they're getting closer."

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones, Colts' Latest Stance Ahead of Deadline
articles.summary: In the final hours before the NFL trade deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts are the epicenter of the league with teams looking at Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones as a potential targets.
articles.body:
In the final hours before the NFL trade deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts are the epicenter of the league with teams looking at Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones as a potential targets.

On Tuesday's episode of Get Up , ESPN's Adam Schefter noted clubs are expected to call the Colts about Jones and Taylor throughout the day.

Schefter added the Colts have been "rather standoffish" in trade discussions about both players to this point, but that could be posturing with the organization "waiting for this day" to potentially maximize their return if any deal comes together.

Jones' situation is interesting because the Colts have reportedly told their veteran quarterback he won't be traded.

Schefter did point out the Minnesota Vikings' sense of urgency might have increased after Carson Wentz struggled in a 23-6 loss against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night.

Wentz finished 8-of-25 for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions. Kyler Murray, who sat out due to a hamstring injury, ranks 27th out of 31 qualified starters in QBR this season.

Jones hasn't exactly impressed in nine starts for the Colts this season with more interceptions (10) than touchdowns (six), but he is at least familiar with Minnesota's offense after finishing the 2024 season with the club.

Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday the Colts had an offer of a second-round draft pick plus additional compensation for Taylor.

Indianapolis has reportedly been seeking at least a second-round draft pick for Taylor, but there is no indication at this point that a deal is close.

The Vikings, New York Giants and Denver Broncos have been most frequently linked to Taylor if the Colts trade him.

Jones would seem easier to move than Taylor because of the finances involved for both players. Jones' $10.51 million in guaranteed money for next season doesn't take effect until the fifth day of the 2027 league year.

Taylor, who signed a two-year, $44 million extension in August, has cap hits over $20 million in 2027 and 2028. He's the only running back with a cap number of at least $20 million in each of the next two years.

Indianapolis (2-7) has lost five straight and has lost 14 of 16 games dating back to last season. Chris Ballard was fired on Oct. 19 midway through his 10th season as general manager.

Ed Dodds replaced Ballard as general manager on an interim basis. He has already traded away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, bringing back a total of three draft picks, including two in 2027.

The Colts currently have 10 picks in the upcoming draft, though no first-rounder because they traded it to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner deal last year.

articles.title: Tom Brady's $110 million Raiders investment could now be worth $515 million as NFL franchise hits $10.3 billion valuation
articles.summary: Tom Brady spent 23 seasons building one of the greatest careers in NFL history. But retirement did not mean he was ready to walk away from football.
articles.body: Tom Brady spent 23 seasons building one of the greatest careers in NFL history. But retirement did not mean he was ready to walk away from football. The seven-time Super Bowl champion found another way to stay connected to the league by investing in the Las Vegas Raiders. What initially looked like a $110 million business move has turned into an eye-catching financial story. With the franchise now valued at $10.3 billion, Brady's 5% ownership stake could be worth approximately $515 million on paper, highlighting the growing financial appeal of NFL team ownership.Tom Brady invested $110 million to secure a 5% stake in the RaidersTom Brady's journey into NFL ownership was not an overnight decision. His interest in becoming part of the Raiders organization first emerged in 2023, when he began working towards acquiring a minority stake in the franchise.The deal eventually reached its biggest milestone in October 2024. NFL owners unanimously approved Brady and businessman Tom Wagner's purchase of a combined 10% interest in the Raiders. The two investors agreed to pay $220 million, giving each of them a 5% share.According to Sports Business Journal, the transaction also involved an additional payment of approximately $24 million, known as a relocation-related fee or flip tax, connected to the Raiders' move from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020. The investment valued the franchise at around $3.5 billion for the transaction.For Brady, the agreement marked a major change in his relationship with professional football. He had spent years competing against the league's best teams. Now, he had a financial interest in one of its franchises.His personal investment of approximately $110 million also gave him a new business opportunity after his playing career. Rather than limiting his involvement to television appearances and commercial partnerships, Brady became part of the ownership structure of an NFL team.NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell welcomed the move when the league approved the agreement."It's great that Tom Brady wants to invest in the NFL," Goodell said.The approval came after months of discussions among league officials and team owners. It also cleared the way for Brady to begin his next chapter in professional football.Raiders' $10.3 billion valuation puts Brady's investment in focusThe biggest development in Brady's ownership story is the remarkable rise in the Raiders' estimated value.When the franchise received approval for the ownership transaction in 2024, Forbes valued the team at approximately $6.7 billion. At that valuation, Brady's 5% stake would have represented an estimated $335 million.However, the latest Forbes NFL team valuations, calculated in September 2026, place the Raiders at $10.3 billion. The franchise recorded a reported 34% increase in value over one year, making it one of the most valuable teams in professional football.Applying that valuation to Brady's 5% ownership interest produces an estimated figure of $515 million.That is a substantial difference from his original investment of approximately $110 million. The implied increase stands at roughly $405 million.However, the figure needs some context. Forbes uses enterprise value, which includes equity and net debt, in its team valuations. Therefore, the $515 million figure is an illustrative estimate based on the franchise's valuation, not a confirmed market price for Brady's ownership interest.He has not publicly announced a sale of his stake, either. The increase represents estimated value on paper rather than money he has collected.Still, the numbers show why NFL ownership has become an attractive long-term investment for wealthy individuals.Tom Brady faced NFL restrictions because of his Fox Sports roleBrady's entry into the Raiders ownership group came with an unusual challenge. He was also preparing to work as Fox Sports' lead NFL game analyst.The situation raised questions about a possible conflict of interest. As a minority owner of one team, Brady could potentially have access to sensitive information about other franchises through his broadcasting work.The NFL addressed those concerns by placing restrictions on his media responsibilities in August 2024.According to the Associated Press report published by NFL.com, Brady could not attend in-person or online broadcast production meetings. He was also prohibited from accessing other teams' facilities, players and coaches.These restrictions mattered because NFL broadcasters often meet players and coaches before games. They also visit training facilities and attend practices to gather information that helps them prepare their coverage.Brady had to work around those limitations while beginning his broadcasting career alongside play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt.The league also required him to follow rules governing public criticism of officials and other teams. He remained permitted to call Raiders games, but his ownership position meant that his role as an analyst came with additional responsibilities.The arrangement was unusual for someone with Brady's football experience. He had spent decades studying opponents, understanding coaching decisions and preparing for major games. Now, some of the traditional access available to broadcasters was off limits.Despite the restrictions, the NFL eventually approved his ownership bid unanimously, allowing him to continue both roles under the league's conditions.Mark Davis sees Tom Brady as an asset beyond his investmentThe financial growth of the Raiders is only one part of the story. Brady's involvement also brings considerable football experience and public attention to the organization.Raiders majority owner Mark Davis has an opportunity to benefit from Brady's understanding of the game. The former quarterback spent 23 seasons in the NFL, winning seven Super Bowls with the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.His experience could prove useful as the franchise works towards long-term stability, particularly at the quarterback position.The Raiders have also benefited from their move to Las Vegas, where Allegiant Stadium gives the organization access to a major entertainment and tourism market. The team's commercial appeal, revenue streams and brand recognition all contribute to its rising valuation.Forbes' September 2026 figures place the franchise's revenue at approximately $887 million, with operating income of $191 million. Those numbers offer further insight into why the Raiders have become such a valuable NFL property.Brady also brings a familiar face to the franchise's growing business profile. His success on the field, media presence and commercial partnerships have made him one of the most recognisable figures in American sports.His Raiders investment therefore represents more than a financial interest in a football team. It gives him a chance to influence the sport from a different position.After years of chasing championships as a quarterback, Brady now has a different challenge. His estimated $110 million investment could be worth around $515 million based on the Raiders' latest valuation. Whether that paper gain grows further will depend on the franchise's future performance and the changing economics of the NFL.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Addresses George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr. Injury Speculation After Colts Game
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones denied Tuesday that the contract statuses of wide receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. played a role in either missing Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones denied Tuesday that the contract statuses of wide receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. played a role in either missing Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Jones addressed the speculation during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan (h/t ESPN's Todd Archer ), saying, "[It's] 100 percent injury related. Put it to rest."

Pickens missed Dallas' 27-23 road victory with shoulder and hamstring injuries, while Porter did not play due to an ankle ailment.

Per Archer , Pickens first suffered the shoulder injury against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Oct. 8, and the hamstring issue popped up over the past two weeks.

As for Porter, he has been hampered by his ankle for "the past few weeks," and left the Cowboys' 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 1 because of it.

Both Pickens and Porter are currently slated to become free agents at the conclusion of the season, which likely contributed to talk of something other than injuries playing a role in them not playing on Sunday.

The Cowboys acquired Pickens in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers prior to the 2025 season, and he went on to have a career year, earning Pro Bowl honors after recording 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns.

Pickens has clearly been behind CeeDee Lamb in the pecking order this season, though, resulting in more modest numbers to the tune of 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns in eight games.

The Cowboys struck another deal with the Steelers this season, acquiring Porter on Sept. 30.

Porter has been hampered by injuries since the trade, though, limiting him to four games, during which he has registered eight tackles and three passes defended.

Like Pickens, the Cowboys did not sign Porter to a new contract when they acquired him, meaning he could potentially hit the open market during the offseason.

While it has been a roller-coaster season for the Cowboys thus far, they are second in the NFC East with a 4-5 record, trailing only the 5-2-1 New York Giants.

Dallas will likely need Pickens and Porter to play significant roles down the stretch in order to make a playoff run, and Jones' comments suggest that their impending free agency won't be part of the decision-making process regarding whether they play.

articles.title: Jordan Love: Green Bay Packers quarterback is fearless and can lead Matt LaFleur's team to Super Bowl, says Neil Reynolds
articles.summary: Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds hails the form of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers in his weekly column; the Packers improved to 6-3 on the year on Sunday with a dominant win over the New England Patriots to continue their march towards the NFL playoffs
articles.body:
But I'm now starting to believe the Green Bay Packers can make a serious run and they have emerged as true contenders in the NFC.

Sunday's 45-27 win over the New England Patriots in Foxborough was a statement victory and it was a win that showed the Packers to be a complete team.

Jordan Love is playing as well as any quarterback in the NFL this season and he backed it up on Sunday on a big stage in a game being called by Tom Brady as he threw for 372 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.

He could not look more comfortable right now. He's in his bag, he's playing with confidence, he's playing calmly and it looks like he has no fear.

That's what's incredible when you look at the success of Jordan Love. It's not dinking and dunking, it is attacking downfield at a more prolific rate than any other quarterback in the NFL.

And he has the guys that can make the plays on the other end. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson both went over 150 receiving yards on Sunday and they both have emerged as true game-breaking wide receivers.

Now you could say that Golden went into Week Nine leading the NFL with seven drops but then look at some of the catches he's tried to make. Again I think it goes back to that aggressive nature of the Packers.

He's not catching 10-yard curl routes or 10-yard crossers over the middle. He's quite often having to track a football that's traveling 50 or 60 yards in the air with the defensive back draped all over him.

So it wasn't that long ago we looked at the Packers with four or five wide receiver targets and said they've got a collection of players but they don't have a true number one. Well they might have something approaching two number ones now in Watson and Golden.

Defensively I felt like they've been dangerous all year and they showed it on Sunday, pouncing early for the interception of Drake Maye - who regressed on a huge stage. Of all the days for Drake Maye to have a nightmare, Tom Brady's calling the game up in the booth - a reminder of the gigantic shoes to fill in New England.

But this is what the Packers do on defense. They rush the passer really well. They harass teams into mistakes and then they are opportunistic. Four takeaways on Sunday was no fluke.

What they did in Foxborough was what they've done all season long, and they still have one of the most prolific pass rushers in the game to return providing Micah Parsons comes back at full speed.

He has taken his time coming back from the knee injury and should be targeting a Thanksgiving week (3:03) return to action.

If that boost comes at the right time then I think the Packers have all the tools to make a serious run come January and I think they're more than capable, based on what we've seen in the last couple of weeks, of extending that run all the way into February and you know what that means - the Super Bowl.

articles.title: Grade the trade: 49ers get some veteran receiver help by trading Colts for Keenan Allen
articles.summary: The Colts got a late-round pick for Allen in the trade.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are winning in spite of numerous injuries, especially at the receiver position.

The 49ers got some help at receiver before the trade deadline without giving up too much.

San Francisco went and got veteran Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts, who have been one of the major sellers before the deadline. The cost was a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Colts, according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer.

The 49ers have been without Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson for most of the season, and Mike Evand and Deebo Samuel have also missed recent games. The 49ers were hoping to get No. 1 receiver Evans back after the bye but he wasn't ready, and that was a sign that they needed some depth at receiver for the rest of the season.

Allen isn't still the star he was with the Chargers earlier in his career, but he still knows how to get open and command targets. He had 40 catches for 351 yards in eight games with the Colts. At age 34, he has played in many offensive schemes and presumably should be able to contribute quickly for the 49ers. There weren't many star receivers available at the trade deadline so the 49ers decided on a value option for depth. It's not a splashy move but it made complete sense.

Once the Colts decided to start selling, it didn't make much sense to hold onto a solid receiver near the end of his career.

The Colts got the selling spree going by trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. While they had other big pieces who were reportedly on the block, grabbing a sixth-round pick for Allen was an obvious move.

That sixth-round pick is very unlikely to move the needle too much on what is going to be a long Colts rebuild, but it was fine value for a player the Colts had no more use for in a lost season.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza, Ashton Jeanty, More Raiders Fantasy Outlook After Kirk Cousins Traded to Vikings
articles.summary: The Fernando Mendoza Era is underway in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
The Fernando Mendoza Era is underway in Las Vegas.

The Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday ahead of the NFL trade deadline for a third-round pick, clearing the way for the 2026 top overall pick to move into the starting role.

And there are obviously plenty of questions about what it means for the fantasy prospects of several players going forward.

We start with Mendoza, who is obviously tough to trust for anybody outside of two-quarterback formats. We haven't seen Mendoza play much outside of garbage time, he doesn't exactly have an elite group of pass-catchers outside of Brock Bowers and the first two matchups of his career will be against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, two very good defenses.

Mendoza should be rostered in all formats (unless you are happy with your current options, obviously), especially considering the schedule eases up substantially after his first two matchups. But you're scratching off a lottery ticket here, not adding a safe bet. Roster him if you have the room, keep him on the bench and see how it all shakes out.

The aforementioned Bowers should remain fantasy's elite tight end. Tight ends tend to be a young quarterback's best friend and the Raiders are very good at generating touches for Bowers. He shouldn't be affected too much by the change.

Running back Ashton Jeanty remains a real enigma. Last week he wasn't a complete afterthought in the run game, splitting carries down the middle with Malik Washington, but he still only managed six rushes for 25 yards. He has remained a reliable option in PPR formats, with 42 catches on the season (the most among running backs in football).

As a checkdown option for Mendoza, there's upside here, but it's fairly limited. He's a flex consideration only at this point.

Finally, Tre Tucker is the player who could be hurt the most by this move, though the Raiders' lack of dynamic pass-catchers plays in his favor. Tucker had developed a nice rapport with Cousins, even if he was a bit boom-or-bust from a fantasy perspective.

Obviously it's unknown what his connection will be like with Mendoza, but the team's lack of other dynamic playmakers at receiver keeps him in the flex conversation.

articles.title: The Vikings may have acquired the only missing piece for their Super Bowl run
articles.summary: After another week of uninspiring quarterback play, the Minnesota Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders. He could be the missing piece in a Super Bowl run.
articles.body: What’s old is new again for the Minnesota Vikings. After another week of uninspiring quarterback play, the Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders on Tuesday, reuniting Cousins with the team he played for from 2018 through 2023. Minnesota is 6-2 this season, with a defense that’s playing at a championship level. But the Vikings’ offense has lagged far behind, and now Minnesota is turning to Cousins, the same quarterback the team spent the last two-plus seasons trying to upgrade from. While they’ve struggled all season, the Vikings’ offense sunk to its nadir on Monday, when backup quarterback Carson Wentz had a miserable performance in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Wentz completed only eight of 25 passes for paltry 81 yards and two interceptions in the loss. Wentz’s passer rating (8.9) and QBR (2.3) were both in the single digits. But offense has been an issue for the Vikings no matter who has been under center. Through nine weeks, Minnesota’s 12 touchdowns are the second-fewest in the entire NFL. Even the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans, both 1-7, have scored more touchdowns than the Vikings. Minnesota’s offense is second-to-last in expected points added per play, per RBSDM, an advanced analytics website. The Vikings are also 29th in EPA per dropback and dropback success rate. Kyler Murray, the former No. 1 overall pick signed to solve the team’s quarterback woes, has been middling at best. His 88.6 passer rating is on par with his five starts last season for the Arizona Cardinals, who effectively benched Murray for journeyman Jacoby Brissett. Murray’s 45.7 QBR is a career-low mark, and is 27th among quarterbacks this season. To make matters worse, former Minnesota quarterbacks have looked better elsewhere. Sam Darnold famously led the Vikings to a 14-3 record in 2024, but after he struggled down the stretch and played poorly in the playoffs, the team let him leave as a free agent. Darnold led the Seahawks to a Super Bowl win last season, and though his play hasn’t been great this year, he has more passing touchdowns in six-plus games than Minnesota does in eight. Meanwhile, J.J. McCarthy, whom the Vikings selected in the first round in 2024 and then made the starter in 2025 before trading him this season, has also played well in limited action. In four games with the New York Giants, McCarthy has a higher passer rating (91.7) and QBR (50.0) than Murray. And then there’s Cousins, who first signed with Minnesota as a free agent in 2018. He started 88 games for the Vikings, posting a 50-37-1 record. Cousins’ time in Minnesota was his most successful on an individual level, as he threw for 171 touchdowns and 55 interceptions with a 101.2 passer rating, but he won only one playoff game in his six seasons. Cousins led the Vikings to a 14-3 record in 2022, then tore his Achilles after eight starts the following season, and Minnesota parted ways with him as it sought an upgrade. But between free agency (Darnold), the draft (McCarthy) and rehabilitation projects (Murray), the Vikings have failed to find an answer. This season, Cousins performed admirably for the Raiders, keeping the starting seat warm for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. In nine starts, Cousins has thrown for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. His 62.8 QBR is 12th-best in the NFL. Meanwhile, despite its 6-2 record, Minnesota is only in fifth place in the NFC playoff picture through nine weeks. The Vikings play in the loaded NFC North, which would have all four teams reach the playoffs if the season ended today. The other offenses in the division — the Detroit Lions, Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears — are all ranked in the top 12 in EPA per play. On the other hand, Minnesota’s defense is ranked first in EPA per play. If Cousins can merely maintain the same level of performance he did in Las Vegas, then the Vikings may have made the most consequential move of the trade deadline — and perhaps even tilted Super Bowl odds in their favor.

articles.title: Josh Downs Traded to Chiefs, New NFL Rumors Reveal Colts' Draft Pick Return Ahead of Deadline
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have taken advantage of the Indianapolis Colts' ongoing roster teardown by bolstering their receiving corps.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs have taken advantage of the Indianapolis Colts' ongoing roster teardown by bolstering their receiving corps.

The Colts traded wideout Josh Downs to the Chiefs Tuesday in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks, according to The Ringer and Netflix's Tom Pelissero .

Downs is playing this season under a $4.2 million cap hit on his expiring rookie contract.

The 25-year-old wideout requested a trade from the Colts ahead of Week 8, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

The Colts, which were 2-5 at the time, had already made their deadline position clear by trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner.

Indianapolis has since also traded Keenan Allen as part of the team's ongoing roster teardown.

Downs has served as the team's slot receiver amid the heel injury that has sidelined Alec Pierce for most of the season. While dealing with extra attention from opposing defenses in Pierce's absence, Downs recorded 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown in nine games prior to his trade.

The fourth-year wideout will hope leaving Indianapolis for a wide receiver room led by Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy will give him an opportunity to increase his production down the stretch of the season.

The biggest question for the Colts will now be what direction the franchise should take after dismissing former general manager Chris Ballard before reportedly turning down offers for Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor ahead of the deadline.

The Chiefs were looking to add wide receiver depth at the deadline after losing Rice and Tyquan Thornton to injury early in the season. The team has often leaned on Kenneth Walker III and their run game during the team's 6-2 start to the 2026 campaign.

Kansas City could hope the addition of Downs, the recent return of Rice and the eventual recovery of Thornton will take some pressure off Walker and bolster the depth around Mahomes in time for a playoff run this winter.
